title.zh: 卷八十五 列傳第七十三: 節義
title.en: Volume 85 Biographies 73: Exemplars of the Loyal and Righteous

sentences.zh: 列傳第七十三節義

translations.literal: Biographies 73: Loyalty and Righteousness
translations.idiomatic: Biography 73: Exemplars of Loyalty and Righteousness

sentences.zh: 于什門段進石文德汲固王玄威婁提劉渴侯硃長生于提馬八龍門文愛晁清劉侯仁石祖興邵洪哲王榮世胡小彪孫道登李幾張安祖王閭劉業興蓋俊郭琰遝龍超乙速孤佛保李棠杜叔毗劉弘游元張須陀楊善會盧楚劉子翊堯君素陳孝意張季珣杜松贇郭世俊郎方貴

translations.literal: Yu Shimen, Duan Jin, Shi Wende, Ji Gu, Wang Xuanwei, Lou Ti, Liu Kehou, Zhu Changsheng, Yu Ti, Ma Balong, Men Wen'ai, Chao Qing, Liu Houran, Shi Zuxing, Shao Hongzhe, Wang Rongshi, Hu Xiaobiao, Sun Daodeng, Li Ji, Zhang Anzu, Wang Lü, Liu Yexing, Gai Jun, Guo Yan, Da Longchao, Yisu Gubao, Li Tang, Du Shupi, Liu Hong, You Yuan, Zhang Xuotuo, Yang Shanhui, Lu Chu, Liu Ziyi, Yao Junsu, Chen Xiaoyi, Zhang Jixun, Du Songyun, Guo Shijun, Lang Fanggui
translations.idiomatic: Yu Shimen, Duan Jin, Shi Wende, Ji Gu, Wang Xuanwei, Lou Ti, Liu Kehou, Zhu Changsheng, Yu Ti, Ma Balong, Men Wen'ai, Chao Qing, Liu Houran, Shi Zuxing, Shao Hongzhe, Wang Rongshi, Hu Xiaobiao, Sun Daodeng, Li Ji, Zhang Anzu, Wang Lü, Liu Yexing, Gai Jun, Guo Yan, Da Longchao, Yisu Gubao, Li Tang, Du Shupi, Liu Hong, You Yuan, Zhang Xuotuo, Yang Shanhui, Lu Chu, Liu Ziyi, Yao Junsu, Chen Xiaoyi, Zhang Jixun, Du Songyun, Guo Shijun, and Lang Fanggui

sentences.zh: 《易》稱：「立人之道，曰仁與義。」

translations.literal: The Book of Changes says: "The way to establish a person is called benevolence and righteousness."
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Changes states: "The way to establish humanity lies in benevolence and righteousness.

sentences.zh: 蓋士之成名，在斯二者。

translations.literal: For a gentleman to achieve a name, it lies in these two.
translations.idiomatic: A gentleman's reputation, it is clear, rests upon these two virtues.

sentences.zh: 故古人以天下為大，方身則輕；

translations.literal: Therefore the ancients regarded the realm as great and their own person as light;
translations.idiomatic: The ancients therefore held the realm to be weighty and their own persons slight;

sentences.zh: 生為重矣，比義則輕。

translations.literal: life was deemed weighty, yet compared with righteousness it was light.
translations.idiomatic: life they counted precious, yet set beside righteousness it grew light.

sentences.zh: 然則死有重於太山，貴其理全也；

translations.literal: Thus death may be heavier than Mount Tai, prized when its principle is complete;
translations.idiomatic: Thus death may outweigh Mount Tai, when its principle is whole and honored;

sentences.zh: 生有輕於鴻毛，重其義全也。

translations.literal: life may be lighter than a goose feather, valued when its righteousness is complete.
translations.idiomatic: and life may prove lighter than a goose feather, when its righteousness is whole and prized.

sentences.zh: 故生無再得，死不可追。

translations.literal: Therefore life cannot be gained twice, and death cannot be recalled.
translations.idiomatic: Life comes but once; death cannot be undone.

sentences.zh: 而仁道不遠，則殺身以徇；

translations.literal: When the way of benevolence is not far, one gives up one's life to follow it;
translations.idiomatic: When the path of benevolence lies near at hand, men lay down their lives to follow it;

sentences.zh: 義重於生，則捐軀而踐。

translations.literal: when righteousness outweighs life, one casts aside the body to tread it.
translations.idiomatic: when righteousness outweighs life itself, they cast aside their bodies to walk it.

sentences.zh: 龍逢殞命于夏癸，比干竭節于商辛，申蒯斷臂于齊莊，弘演納肝于衛懿，漢之紀信、欒布，晉之向雄、嵇紹，並不憚於危亡，以蹈忠貞之節。

translations.literal: Long Feng lost his life under Xia Gui, Bi Gan exhausted his integrity under Shang Xin, Shen Kui severed his arm under Qi Zhuang, Hong Yan offered his liver to Wei Yi; of Han, Ji Xin and Luan Bu; of Jin, Xiang Xiong and Ji Shao—all did not fear peril and ruin, treading the integrity of loyalty and constancy.
translations.idiomatic: Long Feng perished under Jie of Xia, Bi Gan gave his all under Zhou of Shang, Shen Kui severed his arm for Duke Zhuang of Qi, and Hong Yan laid his liver before Duke Yi of Wei; in Han there were Ji Xin and Luan Bu, in Jin Xiang Xiong and Ji Shao—all alike unafraid of ruin, each treading the path of steadfast loyalty.

sentences.zh: 雖功未存於社稷，力無救於顛墜。

translations.literal: Although their achievements were not preserved for the state altars, their strength could not save the tottering realm.
translations.idiomatic: Though their deeds did not preserve the altars of state, nor their strength arrest a realm in collapse,

sentences.zh: 然視彼苟免之徒，貫三光而洞九泉矣。

translations.literal: yet compared with those who sought merely to save themselves, they pierced the three luminaries and illumined the nine springs.
translations.idiomatic: beside those who merely sought to save themselves they pierced sun, moon, and stars and lit the depths of the underworld.

sentences.zh: 凡在立名之士，莫不庶幾焉。

translations.literal: All gentlemen who sought to establish a name looked up to this.
translations.idiomatic: Every man who aspired to leave a name behind looked up to such examples.

sentences.zh: 然至臨難忘身，見危授命，雖斯文不墜，而行之蓋寡。

translations.literal: Yet when it came to facing danger and forgetting self, to meeting peril and surrendering life—though this culture did not fall, those who acted on it were few.
translations.idiomatic: Yet to face peril and forget oneself, to meet crisis and surrender one's life—though the teaching itself never fell, those who truly lived it were scarce indeed.

sentences.zh: 固知士之所重，信在慈乎。

translations.literal: Clearly one knows what the gentleman values: trust lies in constancy, does it not?
translations.idiomatic: One sees plainly what the gentleman holds dear: is it not constancy of heart?

sentences.zh: 非夫內懷鐵石之心，外負陵霜之節，孰能行之若命，赴蹈如歸者乎！

translations.literal: Unless one bore iron and stone within and frost-resisting integrity without, who could act on it as fate and rush to death as if returning home!
translations.idiomatic: Without iron and stone in the breast and frost-defying integrity without, who could treat such duty as fate itself and go to death as if homeward bound!

sentences.zh: 自魏訖隋，年餘二百，若乃歲寒見松柏，疾風知勁草，千載之後，懍懍猶生。

translations.literal: From Wei through Sui, more than two hundred years—if in cold years one sees pine and cypress, in fierce wind one knows tough grass, a thousand years hence they still seem sternly alive.
translations.idiomatic: From Wei through Sui spans more than two hundred years; yet as cold seasons reveal pine and cypress and fierce winds expose tough grass, a thousand years on these men still seem vividly, sternly alive.

sentences.zh: 豈獨聞彼伯夷，懦夫立志，亦冀將來君子，有所庶幾。

translations.literal: Is it only upon hearing of Boyi that the coward resolves himself? One also hopes future gentlemen may aspire likewise.
translations.idiomatic: It is not only on hearing of Boyi that cowards take heart; one also hopes gentlemen yet to come may find something here to emulate.

sentences.zh: 《魏書》序於什門、段進、石文德、汲固、王玄威、婁提、劉渴侯、硃長生、馬八龍、門文愛、晁清、劉侯仁、石祖興、邵洪哲、王榮世、胡小彪、孫道登、李幾、張安祖、王閭以為《節義傳》，今又檢得郭琰、遝龍超、乙速孤佛保，及《周書孝節傳》李棠、杜叔毗附之。

translations.literal: The History of Wei arranged Shimen, Duan Jin, Shi Wende, Ji Gu, Wang Xuanwei, Lou Ti, Liu Kehou, Zhu Changsheng, Ma Balong, Men Wen'ai, Chao Qing, Liu Houran, Shi Zuxing, Shao Hongzhe, Wang Rongshi, Hu Xiaobiao, Sun Daodeng, Li Ji, Zhang Anzu, and Wang Lü as the "Treatise on Loyalty and Righteousness"; now Guo Yan, Da Longchao, and Yisu Gubao have also been found and added, along with Li Tang and Du Shupi from the Zhou History's "Treatise on Filial Loyalty."
translations.idiomatic: The History of Wei grouped Yu Shimen, Duan Jin, Shi Wende, Ji Gu, Wang Xuanwei, Lou Ti, Liu Kehou, Zhu Changsheng, Ma Balong, Men Wen'ai, Chao Qing, Liu Houran, Shi Zuxing, Shao Hongzhe, Wang Rongshi, Hu Xiaobiao, Sun Daodeng, Li Ji, Zhang Anzu, and Wang Lü in its "Loyalty and Righteousness" memoir; here we have also recovered Guo Yan, Da Longchao, and Yisu Gubao, and appended Li Tang and Du Shupi from the Zhou History's memoir on filial loyalty.

sentences.zh: 又案《齊書》不立此篇，而《隋書》序劉弘、皇甫誕、游元、馮慈明、張須阤、楊善會、獨孤盛、元文都、盧楚、劉子翊、堯君素為《誠節傳》。

translations.literal: Further, the History of Qi did not establish this chapter, whereas the History of Sui arranged Liu Hong, Huangfu Dan, You Yuan, Feng Ciming, Zhang Xutuó, Yang Shanhui, Dugu Sheng, Yuan Wendu, Lu Chu, Liu Ziyi, and Yao Junsu in the "Treatise on Sincere Integrity."
translations.idiomatic: The History of Qi, it should be noted, did not include such a chapter; the History of Sui, by contrast, placed Liu Hong, Huangfu Dan, You Yuan, Feng Ciming, Zhang Xuotuo, Yang Shanhui, Dugu Sheng, Yuan Wendu, Lu Chu, Liu Ziyi, and Yao Junsu in its "Sincere Integrity" memoir.

sentences.zh: 今皇甫誕、馮慈明、獨孤盛、元文都各附其家傳，其餘並附此篇，又檢取《隋書孝義傳》郎方貴、郭世俊亦附之，以備《節文傳》云。

translations.literal: Now Huangfu Dan, Feng Ciming, Dugu Sheng, and Yuan Wendu are each appended to their family biographies; the rest are all attached to this chapter. Lang Fanggui and Guo Shijun have also been taken from the Sui History's "Treatise on Filial Righteousness" and appended, to complete the "Treatise on Loyalty and Culture," as it were.
translations.idiomatic: Huangfu Dan, Feng Ciming, Dugu Sheng, and Yuan Wendu are now each placed in his family biography; the remainder are gathered in this chapter. Lang Fanggui and Guo Shijun have also been drawn from the Sui History's memoir on filial righteousness and added here, so that this chapter on loyalty and righteousness may stand complete.

sentences.zh: 於什門，代人也。

translations.literal: Yu Shimen was a man of Dai.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Shimen was a native of Dai.

sentences.zh: 魏明元時為謁者，使喻馮跋。

translations.literal: In the time of Emperor Mingyuan of Wei he served as usher and was sent to instruct Feng Ba.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Mingyuan of Wei he served as palace usher and was dispatched to announce the imperial will to Feng Ba.

sentences.zh: 及至和龍，住外不入，使謂跋曰：「大魏皇帝有詔，須馮主出受，然後敢入。」

translations.literal: When he reached Helong he lodged outside and would not enter, sending word to Ba: "The Great Wei emperor has an edict; the Lord of Feng must come out to receive it—only then dare I enter."
translations.idiomatic: On reaching Helong he remained outside and refused to enter, sending word to Feng Ba: "The emperor of Great Wei has issued an edict. Your lordship must come out to receive it; only then may I dare enter.

sentences.zh: 跋使人牽逼令入。

translations.literal: Ba had men drag and force him to enter.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Ba had men seize and drag him inside.

sentences.zh: 見跋不拜，跋令人按其項。

translations.literal: Seeing Ba he did not bow; Ba had men press down on his neck.
translations.idiomatic: When he met Feng Ba he did not bow. Feng Ba ordered men to force his head down.

sentences.zh: 什門曰：「馮主拜受詔，吾自以賓主致敬，何須苦見逼也？」

translations.literal: Shimen said: "When the Lord of Feng bows to receive the edict, I myself shall render guest-and-host courtesy—why must you torment me with force?"
translations.idiomatic: Shimen said, "When my lord of Feng bows to receive the edict, I on my own will render the courtesies due between host and guest. Why must you torment me with force?

sentences.zh: 與跋往復，聲氣厲然，初不撓屈。

translations.literal: He and Ba went back and forth, his voice stern, never yielding at first.
translations.idiomatic: He and Feng Ba argued back and forth, his tone fierce throughout, and he never once yielded.

sentences.zh: 既而跋止什門。

translations.literal: Thereafter Ba detained Shimen.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Ba then had Shimen detained.

sentences.zh: 什門於群眾中回身背跋，披褲後襠以辱之。

translations.literal: Shimen turned in the crowd, his back to Ba, pulled down his trousers and exposed his buttocks to shame him.
translations.idiomatic: Before the assembled crowd Shimen turned his back on Feng Ba, dropped his trousers, and exposed his buttocks to shame him.

sentences.zh: 既而拘留，隨身衣裳，敗壞略盡，蟣虱被體。

translations.literal: He was then held in custody; the clothes on his person were ruined almost entirely, and lice covered his body.
translations.idiomatic: Held in confinement thereafter, the clothes on his person rotted away almost entirely and lice swarmed over his body.

sentences.zh: 跋遺以衣服，拒而不受。

translations.literal: Ba sent him clothes; he refused and would not accept.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Ba sent him garments, but he refused them.

sentences.zh: 曆二十四年。

translations.literal: Twenty-four years passed.
translations.idiomatic: Twenty-four years passed in this way.

sentences.zh: 後馮弘上表稱臣，乃送什門歸。

translations.literal: Later Feng Hong submitted a memorial declaring himself a subject, and only then sent Shimen back.
translations.idiomatic: Only when Feng Hong later submitted a memorial declaring himself a vassal was Shimen sent home.

sentences.zh: 拜書侍御史。

translations.literal: He was appointed Attending Censor.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Attending Censor.

sentences.zh: 太武下詔褒美，比之蘇武，賜羊千口、帛千匹，進為上大夫，策告宗廟，班示天下。

translations.literal: Emperor Taiwu issued an edict praising him, comparing him to Su Wu, granting a thousand sheep and a thousand bolts of silk, promoting him to Senior Grand Master, reporting to the ancestral temple, and proclaiming it throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taiwu issued an edict praising him, likening him to Su Wu, and granted him a thousand sheep and a thousand bolts of silk. He was promoted to Senior Grand Master; the achievement was announced at the ancestral temple and proclaimed throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 段進，不知何許人也。

translations.literal: Duan Jin—his origin is unknown.
translations.idiomatic: Duan Jin was a man of unknown origin.

sentences.zh: 太武初，為白道守將。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taiwu's reign he was garrison commander of Baidao.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the reign of Emperor Taiwu he served as garrison commander of Baidao.

sentences.zh: 蠕蠕大檀入塞，圍之，力屈被執。

translations.literal: The Rouran khan Dadan entered the frontier, besieged him, and when his strength failed he was captured.
translations.idiomatic: When the Rouran khan Dadan raided the frontier and besieged him, his strength gave out and he was taken prisoner.

sentences.zh: 進抗聲大罵，遂為賊殺。

translations.literal: Jin shouted defiance and reviled them loudly, and was thereupon killed by the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Duan Jin shouted his defiance and cursed them at the top of his voice, and the enemy killed him.

sentences.zh: 帝湣之，追贈安北將軍，賜爵顯美侯，諡曰莊。

translations.literal: The emperor pitied him, posthumously enfeoffing him as General Who Pacifies the North, granting the title Marquis of Xianmei, with the posthumous name Zhuang.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor mourned him and posthumously appointed him General Who Pacifies the North, enfeoffing him as Marquis of Xianmei with the posthumous name Zhuang.

sentences.zh: 石文德，中山蒲陰人也。

translations.literal: Shi Wende was a man of Puyin in Zhongshan.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Wende was a native of Puyin in Zhongshan.

sentences.zh: 有行義。

translations.literal: He possessed righteous conduct.
translations.idiomatic: He was known for upright conduct.

sentences.zh: 真君初，縣令黃宣在任喪亡。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Zhenjun era the magistrate Huang Xuan died in office.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Zhenjun era the county magistrate Huang Xuan died while still in office.

sentences.zh: 宣單貧，無期親。

translations.literal: Xuan was utterly poor and had no kin within the mourning circle.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Xuan was utterly destitute and had no close kin.

sentences.zh: 文德祖父苗以家財殯葬，持服三年。

translations.literal: Wende's grandfather Miao buried him at family expense and observed mourning for three years.
translations.idiomatic: Wende's grandfather Miao buried him at the family's expense and observed the three-year mourning.

sentences.zh: 奉養宣妻二十餘載，及亡，又衰縗斂祔，率禮無闕。

translations.literal: He supported Xuan's wife for more than twenty years; when she died he again donned mourning garments, encoffined her, and buried her beside her husband, observing the rites without omission.
translations.idiomatic: He supported Huang Xuan's wife for more than twenty years, and when she died he again donned mourning, encoffined her, and buried her beside her husband, observing every rite without lapse.

sentences.zh: 自苗逮文德，刺史守令卒官者，制服送之。

translations.literal: From Miao down to Wende, whenever a provincial inspector or district magistrate died in office, they donned mourning garments and escorted the funeral.
translations.idiomatic: From Miao down through Wende, whenever a provincial inspector or local magistrate died in office, the family donned mourning and saw the funeral through.

sentences.zh: 五世同居，閨門雍睦。

translations.literal: Five generations dwelt together; within the gates harmony prevailed.
translations.idiomatic: Five generations lived under one roof, and harmony reigned within the household.

sentences.zh: 又梁州上言，天水白石縣人趙令安、孟蘭強等四世同居，行著州裏。

translations.literal: Liang Province also reported that Zhao Ling'an, Meng Lanqiang, and others of Baishi County in Tianshui dwelt together for four generations, their conduct renowned in the province.
translations.idiomatic: Liang Province also reported that Zhao Ling'an, Meng Lanqiang, and others of Baishi County in Tianshui had lived together for four generations, their conduct renowned throughout the district.

sentences.zh: 詔並標榜門閭。

translations.literal: An edict ordered plaques erected at their gates.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered commemorative plaques set up at their gates.

sentences.zh: 汲固，東郡梁城人也。

translations.literal: Ji Gu was a man of Liangcheng in Dongjun.
translations.idiomatic: Ji Gu was a native of Liangcheng in Dong Commandery.

sentences.zh: 為兗州從事。

translations.literal: He served as Registrar of Yan Province.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Registrar of Yan Province.

sentences.zh: 刺史李式坐事被收，吏人皆送至河上。

translations.literal: The provincial inspector Li Shi was arrested for an offense; clerks and attendants all escorted him to the river.
translations.idiomatic: The provincial inspector Li Shi was arrested on a charge; clerks and attendants all escorted him as far as the river.

sentences.zh: 時式子憲生始滿月。

translations.literal: At that time Shi's son Xian had just completed his first month.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shi's son Xian was then only one month old.

sentences.zh: 式大言於眾曰：「程嬰、仵臼何如人也？」

translations.literal: Shi spoke loudly before the crowd: "What sort of men were Cheng Ying and Gongsun Wujiu?"
translations.idiomatic: Li Shi cried out before the assembled crowd, "What manner of men were Cheng Ying and Gongsun Wujiu?

sentences.zh: 固曰：「今古豈殊！」

translations.literal: Gu said: "Past and present—how are they different!"
translations.idiomatic: Ji Gu replied, "Past and present—how should they differ?"

sentences.zh: 遂便潛還不顧，徑來入城，於式婦閨抱憲歸藏。

translations.literal: He then slipped back without a backward glance, went straight into the city, entered the women's quarters of Shi's wife, took Xian in his arms, and hid him away.
translations.idiomatic: He then slipped back without a backward glance, went straight into the city, entered Li Shi's wife's inner quarters, took the infant Xian in his arms, and hid him away.

sentences.zh: 及捕者收憲，屬有一婢產男，母以婢兒授之。

translations.literal: When the pursuers came to seize Xian, a maid in the household had just borne a son; the mother gave them the maid's child instead.
translations.idiomatic: When the pursuers came to seize the child, a maid in the household had just borne a son; Li Shi's wife gave them the maid's infant instead.

sentences.zh: 事尋泄，固乃攜憲逃遁，遇赦始歸。

translations.literal: The matter was soon exposed; Gu then fled with Xian, returning only when an amnesty was granted.
translations.idiomatic: The ruse was soon discovered; Ji Gu then fled with young Xian and did not return until an amnesty was proclaimed.

sentences.zh: 憲即為固長育，至十餘歲，恆呼固夫婦為郎婆。

translations.literal: Xian was thereafter raised by Gu to his teens, always calling Gu and his wife "Father-in-law and Mother-in-law."
translations.idiomatic: Xian was thereafter raised by Ji Gu until his teens, always addressing Ji Gu and his wife as "Father-in-law" and "Mother-in-law."

sentences.zh: 後高祐為兗州刺史，嘉固節義，以為主簿。

translations.literal: Later Gao You became Inspector of Yan Province, admired Gu's loyalty and righteousness, and appointed him Chief Clerk.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when Gao You became Inspector of Yan Province, he admired Ji Gu's integrity and appointed him Chief Clerk.

sentences.zh: 王玄威，恆農北陝人也。

translations.literal: Wang Xuanwei was a man of Beishan in Hengnong.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xuanwei was a native of Beishan in Hengnong.

sentences.zh: 獻文崩，玄威立草廬於州城門外，衰裳蔬粥，哭踴無時。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xianwen died, Xuanwei erected a thatched hut outside the provincial city gate, wore hemp mourning and ate plain gruel, weeping and stamping without regard to hour.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xianwen died, Xuanwei built a thatched hut outside the provincial city gate, wore hemp mourning and lived on plain gruel, weeping and stamping the ground without regard to hour.

sentences.zh: 刺史苟頹以事表聞。

translations.literal: The provincial inspector Gou Tui reported the matter to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: The provincial inspector Gou Tui reported the matter to the throne.

sentences.zh: 詔令問狀，云：「先帝澤被蒼生，玄威不勝悲慕，戀心如此，不知禮式。」

translations.literal: An edict ordered inquiry into his condition; he said: "The late emperor's grace covered all living things; Xuanwei cannot bear his grief and longing—his heart clings thus, ignorant of ritual forms."
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered an inquiry; he replied, "The late emperor's grace covered all living things. I cannot bear my grief and longing; my heart clings to him thus, though I know nothing of proper ritual forms.

sentences.zh: 詔問玄威，欲有所訴，聽為表列。

translations.literal: The edict asked Xuanwei whether he wished to present any petition and permitted him to set it forth in a memorial.
translations.idiomatic: The edict asked whether Xuanwei wished to present any petition and permitted him to set it forth in a memorial.

sentences.zh: 玄威云：「聞諱悲號，竊謂臣子同例，無所求謁。」

translations.literal: Xuanwei said: "On hearing the taboo name I wail in grief; I privately consider that subject and minister share the same rule—there is nothing I seek to petition."
translations.idiomatic: Xuanwei replied, "On hearing the tabooed name I wail in grief. I consider that subject and minister share the same obligation; I have nothing to petition for.

sentences.zh: 及至百日，乃自竭家財，設四百人齋會。

translations.literal: When the hundredth day came he exhausted his family wealth to hold a vegetarian feast for four hundred persons.
translations.idiomatic: When the hundredth day of mourning arrived he exhausted his family's wealth to hold a vegetarian feast for four hundred persons.

sentences.zh: 忌日，又設百僧供。

translations.literal: On the anniversary he again provided offerings for a hundred monks.
translations.idiomatic: On the anniversary of the death he again provided offerings for a hundred monks.

sentences.zh: 至大除日，詔送白槹褲褶一具與玄威釋服，下州令表異焉。

translations.literal: On the day of the great removal of mourning, an edict sent one set of white hemp trousers and jacket for Xuanwei to lay aside mourning; the order went down to the province to record his exceptional conduct.
translations.idiomatic: On the day when the full mourning period ended, an edict sent him a set of white hemp trousers and jacket so that he might lay mourning aside, and ordered the province to record his exceptional conduct.

sentences.zh: 婁提，代人也。

translations.literal: Lou Ti was a man of Dai.
translations.idiomatic: Lou Ti was a native of Dai.

sentences.zh: 獻文時，為內三郎。

translations.literal: In the time of Emperor Xianwen he served as Inner Third-Rank Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Xianwen he served as Inner Third-Rank Attendant.

sentences.zh: 獻文暴崩，提謂人曰：「聖主升遐，安用活為！」

translations.literal: When Emperor Xianwen died suddenly, Ti said to others: "The sage ruler has ascended afar—what use is living!"
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xianwen died suddenly, Lou Ti said to those around him, "The sage ruler has departed—what use is there in living on?

sentences.zh: 遂引佩刀自刺，幾死。

translations.literal: He then drew his girdle dagger and stabbed himself, nearly dying.
translations.idiomatic: He then drew the dagger at his belt and stabbed himself, nearly dying.

sentences.zh: 文明太后詔賜帛二百匹。

translations.literal: Empress Dowager Wenming issued an edict granting two hundred bolts of silk.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Wenming issued an edict granting him two hundred bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 時有敕勒部人蛭拔寅，兄地于坐盜食官馬，依制命死。

translations.literal: At that time a man of the Chile tribe, Zhibayin, whose elder brother Diyu had been sentenced to death for stealing and eating government horses according to statute—
translations.idiomatic: At that time a Chile tribesman named Zhibayin had an elder brother, Diyu, who was sentenced to death for stealing and eating government horses, as the law required.

sentences.zh: 拔寅自誣己殺，兄又云實非弟殺。

translations.literal: Bayin falsely confessed that he himself had killed the horses; the elder brother also said it was in truth not the younger who had killed them.
translations.idiomatic: Zhibayin falsely confessed that he himself had committed the crime, while his brother declared that in truth the younger had not done it.

sentences.zh: 兄弟爭死，辭不能定，孝文昭原之。

translations.literal: The brothers contended over who should die; their statements could not be settled, and Emperor Xiaowen by edict pardoned them.
translations.idiomatic: The brothers each insisted on dying in the other's place; their accounts could not be reconciled, and Emperor Xiaowen pardoned them both by edict.

sentences.zh: 劉渴侯，不知何許人也。

translations.literal: Liu Kehou—his origin is unknown.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Kehou was a man of unknown origin.

sentences.zh: 稟性剛烈。

translations.literal: His nature was stern and fierce.
translations.idiomatic: By nature he was stern and unyielding.

sentences.zh: 太和中，為徐州後軍，以力死戰，眾寡不敵，遂禽。

translations.literal: In the Taihe era he served as Rear Army of Xuzhou, fought to the death with all his strength, was outnumbered, and was captured.
translations.idiomatic: During the Taihe era he served in the rear army of Xuzhou, fought to the death with all his strength, was overwhelmed by superior numbers, and was taken prisoner.

sentences.zh: 瞋目大罵，終不降屈，為賊所殺。

translations.literal: Glaring, he reviled them loudly, never submitting in the end, and was killed by the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Glaring, he cursed them at the top of his voice and never submitted; the enemy killed him.

sentences.zh: 孝文贈立忠將軍、平州刺史、上庸侯，賜絹千匹、穀千斛。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowen posthumously granted him General Who Establishes Loyalty, Inspector of Ping Province, and Marquis of Shangyong, with a gift of a thousand bolts of silk and a thousand hu of grain.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowen posthumously appointed him General Who Establishes Loyalty, Inspector of Ping Province, and Marquis of Shangyong, and granted a thousand bolts of silk and a thousand hu of grain.

sentences.zh: 有嚴季者亦為軍校尉，與渴侯同殿，勢窮被執，終不降屈。

translations.literal: There was also Yan Ji, who served as military school commandant; he was in the same hall as Kehou, his strength exhausted and captured, yet in the end he did not submit.
translations.idiomatic: A certain Yan Ji also served as military school commandant. He fought in the same engagement as Liu Kehou; when his strength gave out he too was captured, yet he never submitted.

sentences.zh: 後得逃還，除立節將軍，賜爵五等男。

translations.literal: Later he escaped and returned, was appointed General Who Establishes Integrity, and was enfeoffed as Baron of the Fifth Rank.
translations.idiomatic: He later escaped and returned, was appointed General Who Establishes Integrity, and was enfeoffed as Baron of the Fifth Rank.

sentences.zh: 硃長生、於提者，並代人也。

translations.literal: Zhu Changsheng and Yu Ti were both men of Dai.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Changsheng and Yu Ti were both natives of Dai.

sentences.zh: 孝文時，長生為員外散騎常侍，與提俱使高車。

translations.literal: In the time of Emperor Xiaowen, Changsheng was Supernumerary Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry and went with Ti as envoy to the Gaoche.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Xiaowen, Changsheng served as Supernumerary Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry and was sent with Yu Ti as envoy to the Gaoche.

sentences.zh: 既至，高車王阿伏至羅責長生等拜，長生拒之。

translations.literal: When they arrived, the Gaoche king Avu Zhiluo demanded that Changsheng and the others bow; Changsheng refused.
translations.idiomatic: On their arrival the Gaoche king Avu Zhiluo demanded that Changsheng and his party bow; Changsheng refused.

sentences.zh: 阿伏至羅乃不以禮待。

translations.literal: Avu Zhiluo then did not treat them with courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: Avu Zhiluo thereupon ceased to treat them with courtesy.

sentences.zh: 長生以金銀寶器奉之，至羅既受獻，長生曰：「為臣內附，宜盡臣禮，何得口雲再拜，而實不拜。」

translations.literal: Changsheng presented him with gold, silver, and precious vessels as tribute; after Zhiluo had accepted the gifts, Changsheng said: "As a subject who has submitted within, you ought to perform the full subject's rites—how can you say with your mouth that you bow twice, yet in fact not bow?"
translations.idiomatic: Changsheng presented gold, silver, and precious vessels as tribute. After Avu Zhiluo had accepted the gifts, Changsheng said, "As a subject who has submitted to the inner court, you ought to observe a subject's full rites. How can you say with your mouth that you bow twice, yet in fact not bow at all?

sentences.zh: 呼出帳，命眾中拜。

translations.literal: He called him out of the tent and ordered him to bow before the assembled multitude.
translations.idiomatic: He called Avu Zhiluo out of the tent and ordered him to bow before the assembled multitude.

sentences.zh: 阿伏至羅慚其臣下，大怒曰：「帳中何不教我拜，而辱我於大眾？」

translations.literal: Avu Zhiluo, shamed before his subjects, raged: "Why did you not teach me to bow inside the tent, yet humiliate me before the great crowd?"
translations.idiomatic: Ashamed before his own followers, Avu Zhiluo flew into a rage. "Why did you not teach me to bow inside the tent," he cried, "yet humiliate me before the whole assembly?

sentences.zh: 奪長生等獻物，內之叢石，兵脅之曰：「為我臣則活，不降則殺汝！」

translations.literal: He seized the gifts of Changsheng and the others, shut them among the rocks, and threatened them with troops: "Become my subjects and live; if you do not submit I shall kill you!"
translations.idiomatic: He seized the envoys' gifts, shut them among the rocks, and threatened them at sword's point: "Become my subjects and live; refuse, and I shall kill you!"

sentences.zh: 長生與於提瞋目厲聲責之曰：「我為鬼，不為汝臣！」

translations.literal: Changsheng and Yu Ti glared, their voices stern, reproaching him: "We shall be ghosts—we will not be your subjects!"
translations.idiomatic: Changsheng and Yu Ti glared at him and cried out in stern reproach, "We shall be ghosts before we become your subjects!"

sentences.zh: 阿伏至羅大怒，絕其飲食。

translations.literal: Avu Zhiluo was greatly enraged and cut off their food and drink.
translations.idiomatic: Avu Zhiluo was furious and cut off their food and drink.

sentences.zh: 從者三十人皆求阿伏至羅，乃給以肉酪。

translations.literal: Their thirty attendants all begged Avu Zhiluo, and he then supplied meat and curds.
translations.idiomatic: Their thirty attendants all pleaded with Avu Zhiluo, and he then supplied them with meat and curds.

sentences.zh: 長生與提又不從，乃各分徙之。

translations.literal: Changsheng and Ti again would not comply, so he had them separated and relocated each in turn.
translations.idiomatic: Changsheng and Yu Ti again refused, so he had them separated and sent to different places.

sentences.zh: 三歲及放還。

translations.literal: After three years they were released and sent back.
translations.idiomatic: After three years they were released and sent home.

sentences.zh: 孝文以長生等守節，遠同蘇武，拜長生河內太守，提隴西太守，並賜爵五等男，從者皆為令長。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowen, because Changsheng and the others kept their integrity, likening them from afar to Su Wu, appointed Changsheng Administrator of Henei and Ti Administrator of Longxi, both enfeoffed as Barons of the Fifth Rank; their attendants all became magistrates.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowen, holding that Changsheng and his companions had kept their integrity in a manner far akin to Su Wu, appointed Changsheng Administrator of Henei and Yu Ti Administrator of Longxi, enfeoffing both as Barons of the Fifth Rank; their attendants were all made district magistrates.

sentences.zh: 馬八龍，武邑武強人也。

translations.literal: Ma Balong was a man of Wuqiang in Wuyi.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Balong was a native of Wuqiang in Wuyi.

sentences.zh: 輕財重義。

translations.literal: He held wealth lightly and prized righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: He held wealth lightly and prized righteousness.

sentences.zh: 友人武遂縣尹靈哲在軍喪亡，八龍聞即奔赴，負屍而歸，以家財殯葬，為制緦麻，撫其孤遺，恩如所生。

translations.literal: His friend Yin Lingzhe of Wusui County died in the army; on hearing this Balong at once rushed thither, carried the corpse back on his shoulders, buried him at family expense, donned the coarsest hemp mourning, and nurtured the orphans left behind with affection as if they were his own children.
translations.idiomatic: When his friend Yin Lingzhe of Wusui County died on campaign, Balong heard the news and rushed to the scene, carried the body home on his shoulders, buried him at his family's expense, donned the coarsest hemp mourning, and raised the orphans left behind with the same devotion he would have shown his own children.

sentences.zh: 州郡表列，詔表門閭。

translations.literal: The province and commandery reported his case; an edict ordered a plaque at his gate.
translations.idiomatic: The province and commandery reported his conduct to the throne, and an edict ordered a commemorative plaque set up at his gate.

sentences.zh: 門文愛，汲郡山陽人也。

translations.literal: Men Wen'ai was a man of Shanyang in Jijun.
translations.idiomatic: Men Wen'ai was a native of Shanyang in Ji Commandery.

sentences.zh: 早孤，供養伯父母以孝謹聞。

translations.literal: Orphaned early, he supported his uncle and aunt and was known for filial care.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned early, he supported his uncle and aunt and was renowned for filial devotion.

sentences.zh: 伯父亡，服未終，伯母又亡。

translations.literal: When his uncle died, before the mourning period had ended his aunt also died.
translations.idiomatic: His uncle died, and before the mourning period had ended his aunt died as well.

sentences.zh: 文愛居喪持服六年，哀毀骨立。

translations.literal: Wen'ai observed mourning and wore the garments for six years, his grief wasting him until only bone remained.
translations.idiomatic: Wen'ai observed mourning for six years, his grief so consuming that he was worn to skin and bone.

sentences.zh: 鄉人魏仲賢等相與標其孝義。

translations.literal: His fellow townsman Wei Zhongxian and others jointly commended his filial righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: His fellow townsman Wei Zhongxian and others jointly commended his filial devotion.

sentences.zh: 晁清，遼東人也。

translations.literal: Chao Qing was a man of Liaodong.
translations.idiomatic: Chao Qing was a native of Liaodong.

sentences.zh: 祖暉，濟州刺史、潁川公。

translations.literal: His grandfather Hui was Inspector of Ji Province and Duke of Yingchuan.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Hui had served as Inspector of Ji Province and Duke of Yingchuan.

sentences.zh: 清襲祖爵，例降為伯。

translations.literal: Qing inherited his grandfather's title, which by regulation was reduced to marquis.
translations.idiomatic: Qing inherited his grandfather's title, which by regulation was reduced to marquis.

sentences.zh: 為梁城戍將，梁師攻圍，糧盡城陷。

translations.literal: He served as garrison commander of Liangcheng; Liang forces besieged it, provisions were exhausted, and the city fell.
translations.idiomatic: He served as garrison commander of Liangcheng. Liang forces besieged the city until provisions ran out and it fell.

sentences.zh: 清抗節不屈，為賊所殺。

translations.literal: Qing resisted with integrity and would not submit, and was killed by the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Chao Qing held firm and refused to submit, and the enemy killed him.

sentences.zh: 宣武褒美，贈樂陵太守，諡曰忠。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuanwu praised him, posthumously granting him Administrator of Leling, with the posthumous name Zhong.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuanwu praised his conduct and posthumously appointed him Administrator of Leling, with the posthumous name Zhong.

sentences.zh: 子榮賓襲。

translations.literal: His son Rongbin inherited.
translations.idiomatic: His son Rongbin inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 劉侯仁，豫州人也。

translations.literal: Liu Houran was a man of Yuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Houran was a native of Yu Province.

sentences.zh: 城人白早生殺刺史司馬悅，據城南叛。

translations.literal: A townsman, Bai Zaosheng, killed the provincial inspector Sima Yue, seized the south of the city, and rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: A townsman named Bai Zaosheng killed the provincial inspector Sima Yue, seized the southern part of the city, and rebelled.

sentences.zh: 悅息朏，走投侯仁，賊雖重加購募，又嚴其捶撻，侯仁終無漏泄。

translations.literal: Yue's son Fei fled to Houran for refuge; though the rebels heaped rewards on informers and subjected him to severe beatings, Houran in the end never divulged anything.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Yue's son Fei fled to Liu Houran for refuge. Though the rebels offered heavy rewards and subjected Houran to severe beatings, he never divulged the boy's whereabouts.

sentences.zh: 朏遂免禍。

translations.literal: Fei thus escaped harm.
translations.idiomatic: Fei thus escaped harm.

sentences.zh: 事寧，有司奏其操行，請免府籍，敘一小縣。

translations.literal: When the affair was settled, the relevant offices reported his conduct and requested that he be removed from the prefectural register and appointed to a small county.
translations.idiomatic: When the affair was settled, the relevant offices reported his conduct and requested that he be struck from the prefectural register and appointed magistrate of a small county.

sentences.zh: 詔可。

translations.literal: The edict approved.
translations.idiomatic: The edict approved.

sentences.zh: 石祖興，常山九門人也。

translations.literal: Shi Zuxing was a man of Jiumen in Changshan.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Zuxing was a native of Jiumen in Changshan.

sentences.zh: 太守田文彪、縣令和真等喪亡，祖興自出家絹二百餘匹，營護喪事。

translations.literal: When the Administrator Tian Wenbiao, the Magistrate He Zhen, and others died, Zuxing on his own contributed more than two hundred bolts of silk from the family and managed their funerals.
translations.idiomatic: When the Administrator Tian Wenbiao, the Magistrate He Zhen, and others died, Zuxing contributed more than two hundred bolts of silk from his family's stores and saw to their funerals.

sentences.zh: 州郡表列。

translations.literal: The province and commandery reported his case.
translations.idiomatic: The province and commandery reported his conduct to the throne.

sentences.zh: 孝文嘉之，賜爵二級為上造。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowen commended him and granted two ranks of nobility, making him Shangzao.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowen commended him and raised him two ranks of nobility to Shangzao.

sentences.zh: 後拜寧陵令，卒。

translations.literal: Later he was appointed Magistrate of Ningling and died in office.
translations.idiomatic: He was later appointed Magistrate of Ningling and died in office.

sentences.zh: 吏部尚書李韶奏其節義，請加贈諡，以獎來者，靈太后如所奏。

translations.literal: Minister of Personnel Li Shao memorialized his loyalty and righteousness and requested an added posthumous title to encourage those who would come after; Empress Dowager Ling approved as memorialized.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shao, Minister of Personnel, memorialized his integrity and requested an added posthumous title to encourage future exemplars; Empress Dowager Ling approved the request.

sentences.zh: 有司諡曰恭。

translations.literal: The relevant offices gave the posthumous name Gong.
translations.idiomatic: The relevant offices gave him the posthumous name Gong.

sentences.zh: 邵洪哲，上谷沮陽人也。

translations.literal: Shao Hongzhe was a man of Juyang in Shanggu.
translations.idiomatic: Shao Hongzhe was a native of Juyang in Shanggu.

sentences.zh: 縣令范道榮先自朐城歸款，以除縣令。

translations.literal: The magistrate Fan Daorong had earlier submitted from Jucheng and was appointed magistrate in recognition.
translations.idiomatic: The magistrate Fan Daorong had earlier surrendered from Jucheng and was appointed magistrate in recognition of his submission.

sentences.zh: 道榮鄉人徐孔明妄經公府，訟道榮非勳，道榮坐除名。

translations.literal: Daorong's fellow townsman Xu Kongming falsely reported him to the government offices, suing that Daorong had no merit; Daorong was dismissed and his name struck from the rolls.
translations.idiomatic: Daorong's fellow townsman Xu Kongming lodged a false complaint at the government offices, alleging that Daorong had no claim to merit; Daorong was dismissed and struck from the rolls.

sentences.zh: 羈旅孤貧，不能自理。

translations.literal: A wanderer, alone and poor, he could not manage for himself.
translations.idiomatic: A wanderer, alone and destitute, he could not manage on his own.

sentences.zh: 洪哲不勝義憤，遂代道榮詣京師，明申曲直，經歷寒暑，不憚劬勞。

translations.literal: Hongzhe, unable to bear righteous indignation, thereupon went to the capital on Daorong's behalf, clearly setting forth right and wrong, passing through cold and heat without fearing toil.
translations.idiomatic: Hongzhe, overcome by righteous indignation, went to the capital on Daorong's behalf, clearly setting forth the rights and wrongs of the case, enduring cold and heat without regard for hardship.

sentences.zh: 道榮卒得復雪。

translations.literal: Daorong in the end had his honor restored.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Daorong's name was at last cleared.

sentences.zh: 又北鎮反亂，道榮孤單，無所歸附。

translations.literal: When the northern garrisons rebelled, Daorong was alone with nowhere to turn.
translations.idiomatic: When the northern garrisons rebelled, Daorong was utterly alone with nowhere to turn.

sentences.zh: 洪哲兄伯川復率鄉人來相迎接，送達幽州。

translations.literal: Hongzhe's elder brother Bochuan again led fellow townsmen to meet and escort him, delivering him to You Province.
translations.idiomatic: Hongzhe's elder brother Bochuan again led fellow townsmen to meet and escort him, delivering him safely to You Province.

sentences.zh: 道榮感其誠節，訴省申聞。

translations.literal: Daorong, moved by their sincere loyalty, reported to the provincial authorities.
translations.idiomatic: Moved by their sincere loyalty, Daorong reported the matter to the provincial authorities.

sentences.zh: 詔下州郡，標其里閭。

translations.literal: An edict went down to the provinces and commanderies to mark their hamlet.
translations.idiomatic: An edict went down to the provinces and commanderies ordering a commemorative plaque for their hamlet.

sentences.zh: 王榮世，陽平館陶人也。

translations.literal: Wang Rongshi was a man of Guantao in Yangping.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Rongshi was a native of Guantao in Yangping.

sentences.zh: 為三城戍主、方城縣子。

translations.literal: He served as garrison commander of Sancheng and Baron of Fangcheng County.
translations.idiomatic: He served as garrison commander of Sancheng and held the title Baron of Fangcheng County.

sentences.zh: 梁師攻圍，力窮，知不可全，乃先焚府庫，後殺妻妾。

translations.literal: Liang forces besieged him; his strength exhausted, knowing the city could not be preserved, he first burned the government storehouses, then killed his wife and concubines.
translations.idiomatic: When Liang forces besieged the city and his strength gave out, knowing it could not be saved, he first burned the government storehouses and then killed his wife and concubines.

sentences.zh: 及賊陷城，與戍副鄧元興等俱以不屈被害。

translations.literal: When the bandits took the city, he and the deputy garrison commander Deng Yuanxing and others were all killed for refusing to submit.
translations.idiomatic: When the enemy took the city, he and the deputy commander Deng Yuanxing and others were all killed for refusing to submit.

sentences.zh: 明帝下詔，褒美忠節，進榮世爵為伯，贈齊州刺史；

translations.literal: Emperor Ming issued an edict praising their loyal integrity, advancing Rongshi's title to marquis and posthumously granting him Inspector of Qi Province;
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming issued an edict praising their steadfast loyalty, promoting Rongshi's title to marquis and posthumously appointing him Inspector of Qi Province;

sentences.zh: 元興開國子，贈洛州刺史。

translations.literal: Yuanxing was enfeoffed as Viscount with a state foundation and posthumously granted Inspector of Luo Province.
translations.idiomatic: Deng Yuanxing was enfeoffed as founding viscount and posthumously appointed Inspector of Luo Province.

sentences.zh: 胡小彪，河南河陰人也。

translations.literal: Hu Xiaobiao was a man of Heyin in Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Xiaobiao was a native of Heyin in Henan.

sentences.zh: 少有武氣。

translations.literal: From youth he had a martial spirit.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he showed a martial spirit.

sentences.zh: 正光末，為統軍于晉壽。

translations.literal: At the end of the Zhengguang era he served as army commander at Jinshou.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Zhengguang era he served as army commander at Jinshou.

sentences.zh: 孝昌中，梁將樊文識等寇邊。

translations.literal: In the Xiaochang era the Liang general Fan Wenshi and others raided the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: During the Xiaochang era the Liang general Fan Wenshi and others raided the frontier.

sentences.zh: 益州刺史邴虯遣長史和安固守小劍，文熾圍之。

translations.literal: The Inspector of Yi Province, Bing Qiu, sent his Chief Clerk He An to hold Xiaojian firmly; Wenchi besieged it.
translations.idiomatic: Bing Qiu, Inspector of Yi Province, sent his Chief Clerk He An to hold Xiaojian; Fan Wenchi besieged the place.

sentences.zh: 虯命小彪與統軍崔珍寶同往防拒。

translations.literal: Qiu ordered Xiaobiao and the army commander Cui Zhenbao to go together to defend against the attack.
translations.idiomatic: Bing Qiu ordered Xiaobiao and the army commander Cui Zhenbao to go together to reinforce the defense.

sentences.zh: 文熾掩襲小彪、珍寶並禽之。

translations.literal: Wenchi launched a surprise attack and captured both Xiaobiao and Zhenbao.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Wenchi launched a surprise attack and captured both Xiaobiao and Zhenbao.

sentences.zh: 文熾攻小劍未陷，乃將珍寶至城下，使謂和安曰：「南軍強盛，北救不來，豈若歸款，取其富貴？」

translations.literal: Wenchi had not yet taken Xiaojian; he brought Zhenbao to the foot of the wall and had him say to He An: "The southern army is strong; northern relief will not come—would it not be better to submit and win wealth and rank?"
translations.idiomatic: Before Xiaojian had fallen, Wenchi brought Zhenbao to the foot of the wall and had him call to He An: "The southern army is strong and northern relief will not come. Would it not be better to submit and win wealth and rank?

sentences.zh: 和安命射之，乃退。

translations.literal: He An ordered archers to shoot at him, and they withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: He An ordered archers to shoot at him, and the enemy withdrew.

sentences.zh: 復逼小彪與和安交言。

translations.literal: They again forced Xiaobiao to speak with He An.
translations.idiomatic: They again forced Xiaobiao to speak with He An.

sentences.zh: 小彪乃慷慨謂安曰：「我柵不防，為賊所虜。

translations.literal: Xiaobiao then spoke fervently to An: "My palisade was not defended and I was captured by the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaobiao then cried out fervently to He An, "My palisade was poorly defended and I was captured by the enemy.

sentences.zh: 觀其兵士，勢不足言，努力堅守，魏行台、傅梁州遣將已至。」

translations.literal: Looking at their troops, their strength is not worth mentioning—strive to hold firm; the Wei executive and Fu, Inspector of Liang, have already sent generals who have arrived."
translations.idiomatic: Look at their troops—their strength is nothing worth speaking of. Hold firm with all your strength; the Wei executive and Fu, Inspector of Liang, have already sent generals who are near at hand.

sentences.zh: 賊以刀毆擊，言不得終，遂害之。

translations.literal: The bandits struck him with blades; he could not finish his words and was thereupon killed.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy struck him with blades before he could finish; they killed him on the spot.

sentences.zh: 三軍無不歎其壯節，哀其死亡。

translations.literal: Throughout the three armies none failed to admire his stalwart integrity and mourn his death.
translations.idiomatic: Throughout the army none failed to admire his stalwart integrity and mourn his death.

sentences.zh: 賊尋奔敗，禽其次將蕭世澄、陳文緒等一十一人。

translations.literal: The bandits soon fled in defeat; eleven of their officers including the deputy generals Xiao Shicheng and Chen Wenxu were captured.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy soon fled in defeat, and eleven of their officers including the deputy generals Xiao Shicheng and Chen Wenxu were captured.

sentences.zh: 行台魏子建壯其氣概，啟以世澄購其屍柩，乃獲骸骨歸葬之。

translations.literal: The executive Wei Zijian admired his spirit; he memorialized that Shicheng be exchanged for his coffin, and thus obtained his remains and returned them for burial.
translations.idiomatic: The executive Wei Zijian admired his spirit and memorialized that Xiao Shicheng be exchanged for his body; the remains were recovered and sent home for burial.

sentences.zh: 遜道登，彭城呂縣人也。

translations.literal: Sun Daodeng was a man of Lü County in Pengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Daodeng was a native of Lü County in Pengcheng.

sentences.zh: 永安初，為梁將韋休等所虜。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Yong'an era he was captured by the Liang general Wei Xiu and others.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Yong'an era he was captured by the Liang general Wei Xiu and his forces.

sentences.zh: 面縛臨刃，巡遠村塢，令其招降鄉曲。

translations.literal: Bound facing the blade, he was led through distant villages and stockades and ordered to induce the local people to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Bound and led before the blade, he was marched through distant villages and stockades and ordered to induce the local people to surrender.

sentences.zh: 道登厲聲唱呼：「但當努力，賊無所能！」

translations.literal: Daodeng shouted in a stern voice: "Only strive with all your strength—the bandits can do nothing!"
translations.idiomatic: Daodeng shouted in a stern voice, "Only strive with all your strength—the enemy can do nothing!

sentences.zh: 賊遂屠戮之。

translations.literal: The bandits thereupon slaughtered him.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy thereupon slaughtered him.

sentences.zh: 又荊州被圍，行台宗靈恩遣使宗女等四人入城曉喻，為賊將所獲。

translations.literal: When Jing Province was besieged, the executive Zong Ling'en sent envoys including Zong Nü and three others into the city to explain and persuade; they were captured by a rebel general.
translations.idiomatic: When Jing Province was besieged, the executive Zong Ling'en sent four envoys including Zong Nü into the city to explain and persuade the defenders; a rebel general captured them.

sentences.zh: 執女等巡城，令其改辭。

translations.literal: Holding the women and the others, they paraded them around the wall and ordered them to change their words.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels paraded them around the wall and ordered them to change their message.

sentences.zh: 女等大言：「天軍垂至，堅守莫降。」

translations.literal: The women cried out loudly: "The imperial army is about to arrive—hold firm and do not surrender."
translations.idiomatic: They cried out loudly, "The imperial army is about to arrive—hold firm and do not surrender!

sentences.zh: 賊忿，各刳其腹，然後斬首。

translations.literal: The bandits in rage disemboweled each of them and then beheaded them.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels in a rage disemboweled each of them and then cut off their heads.

sentences.zh: 二州表其節義。

translations.literal: The two provinces reported their loyal integrity.
translations.idiomatic: The two provinces reported their steadfast loyalty.

sentences.zh: 道登等並賜五品郡、五等子爵，聽子弟承襲，遣使詣所在弔祭。

translations.literal: Daodeng and the others were all granted fifth-rank commandery titles and the rank of viscount of the fifth degree; their sons and younger brothers were permitted to inherit; envoys were sent to the places concerned to offer mourning sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: Daodeng and the others were all granted fifth-rank commandery titles and the rank of viscount of the fifth degree, with permission for sons and younger brothers to inherit; envoys were sent to their home districts to offer mourning sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 李幾，博陵安平人也。

translations.literal: Li Ji was a man of Anping in Boling.
translations.idiomatic: Li Ji was a native of Anping in Boling.

sentences.zh: 七世共居同財。

translations.literal: Seven generations dwelt together and shared property.
translations.idiomatic: Seven generations lived together and shared their property.

sentences.zh: 家有二十二房，一百九十八口，長幼濟濟，風禮著聞。

translations.literal: The household had twenty-two branches and one hundred ninety-eight mouths; old and young thronged in order, their customs and rites renowned.
translations.idiomatic: The household comprised twenty-two branches and one hundred ninety-eight members; old and young thronged in orderly array, and their customs and rites were renowned.

sentences.zh: 至於作役，卑幼競集。

translations.literal: When it came to labor service, the younger members vied to gather.
translations.idiomatic: When labor was required, the younger members all rushed to take part.

sentences.zh: 鄉里嗟美，標其門閭。

translations.literal: The district sighed in admiration and marked their gate.
translations.idiomatic: The district admired them, and a commemorative plaque was set up at their gate.

sentences.zh: 張安祖，河陽人也。

translations.literal: Zhang Anzu was a man of Heyang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Anzu was a native of Heyang.

sentences.zh: 襲世爵山北侯。

translations.literal: He inherited the hereditary title Marquis of Shanbei.
translations.idiomatic: He inherited the hereditary title Marquis of Shanbei.

sentences.zh: 時有元承貴，曾為河陽令。

translations.literal: At that time there was Yuan Chenggui, who had once been Magistrate of Heyang.
translations.idiomatic: At that time there was Yuan Chenggui, who had once served as Magistrate of Heyang.

sentences.zh: 家貧，且赴尚書求選，逢天寒甚，遂凍死路側。

translations.literal: His family was poor; he was on his way to the Ministry of Personnel to seek appointment when the cold was severe, and he froze to death by the roadside.
translations.idiomatic: His family was poor. He was on his way to the Ministry of Personnel to seek appointment when the cold grew fierce, and he froze to death by the roadside.

sentences.zh: 一子年幼，停屍門巷，棺殮無托。

translations.literal: He had one young son; the corpse lay in the lane with no one to provide coffin and burial.
translations.idiomatic: He left a young son; the body lay in the lane with no one to provide a coffin or burial.

sentences.zh: 安祖悲哭盡禮，買木為棺，手自營作，殮殯周給。

translations.literal: Anzu wept in grief and performed the full rites, bought wood for a coffin, worked on it with his own hands, and provided complete encoffinment and burial.
translations.idiomatic: Anzu mourned him with full rites, bought wood for a coffin, fashioned it with his own hands, and saw to the encoffinment and burial in full.

sentences.zh: 朝野嘉歎。

translations.literal: Court and commonalty praised and sighed.
translations.idiomatic: Court and commonalty alike praised his conduct.

sentences.zh: 尚書聞奏，標其門閭。

translations.literal: The Ministry of Personnel heard and reported; his gate was marked.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of Personnel reported the matter to the throne, and a commemorative plaque was set up at his gate.

sentences.zh: 王閭，北海密人也。

translations.literal: Wang Lü was a man of Mi in Beihai.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Lü was a native of Mi in Beihai.

sentences.zh: 數世同居，有百口。

translations.literal: Several generations dwelt together, numbering a hundred mouths.
translations.idiomatic: Several generations lived together under one roof, numbering a hundred members.

sentences.zh: 又太山劉業興，四世同居，魯郡蓋俊，六世同居，並共財產，家門雍睦。

translations.literal: Also Liu Yexing of Taishan dwelt together for four generations; Gai Jun of Lu Commandery dwelt together for six generations—they all shared property, and harmony prevailed within their gates.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yexing of Taishan lived together for four generations; Gai Jun of Lu Commandery for six—they all shared property, and harmony reigned within their households.

sentences.zh: 鄉里敬異。

translations.literal: Their districts revered and marveled at them.
translations.idiomatic: Their districts revered them.

sentences.zh: 有司申奏，皆標門閭。

translations.literal: The relevant offices reported; all their gates were marked.
translations.idiomatic: The relevant offices reported their cases, and commemorative plaques were set up at all their gates.

sentences.zh: 遝龍超，晉壽人也。

translations.literal: Da Longchao was a man of Jinshou.
translations.idiomatic: Da Longchao was a native of Jinshou.

sentences.zh: 性尚義俠，少為鄉里所重。

translations.literal: By nature he prized righteousness and chivalry; from youth he was esteemed in his district.
translations.idiomatic: By nature he prized righteousness and chivalry, and from youth his district held him in esteem.

sentences.zh: 永熙中，梁將樊文熾來寇益州，刺史傅和孤城固守。

translations.literal: In the Yongxi era the Liang general Fan Wenchi came to raid Yi Province; the Inspector Fu He held the isolated city in a firm defense.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yongxi era the Liang general Fan Wenchi invaded Yi Province, and the Inspector Fu He held the isolated city in a desperate defense.

sentences.zh: 龍超每出戰，輒破之。

translations.literal: Whenever Longchao went out to battle he invariably defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Longchao went out to fight he invariably routed the enemy.

sentences.zh: 時攻圍既久，糧矢方盡，刺史遣龍超夜出，請援於漢中，遂為文熾所得。

translations.literal: The siege had already lasted long; grain and arrows were nearly exhausted; the inspector sent Longchao out by night to seek relief from Hanzhong, and he was thereupon captured by Wenchi.
translations.idiomatic: The siege had dragged on until grain and arrows were nearly spent. The inspector sent Longchao out by night to seek relief from Hanzhong, and Fan Wenchi captured him.

sentences.zh: 許以封爵，使告城中曰：「外無援軍，宜早降。」

translations.literal: They promised him enfeoffment and had him tell the city: "There are no relief troops outside—you should surrender early."
translations.idiomatic: They promised him a title and rank and had him call to the city, "There are no relief troops outside. You should surrender at once.

sentences.zh: 乃置龍超於攻樓上。

translations.literal: They then placed Longchao on the assault tower.
translations.idiomatic: They placed Longchao on the assault tower.

sentences.zh: 龍超乃告刺史曰：「援軍數萬，近在大寒。」

translations.literal: Longchao then told the inspector: "Relief troops number in the tens of thousands and are near at Dahan.
translations.idiomatic: Longchao then called to the inspector, "Relief troops number in the tens of thousands and are close at hand.

sentences.zh: 文熾大怒，火炙殺之。

translations.literal: Wenchi was greatly enraged and had him killed by roasting over fire.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Wenchi flew into a rage and had him burned alive.

sentences.zh: 至死，辭氣不撓。

translations.literal: Until death his words and bearing did not bend.
translations.idiomatic: To the end his bearing and speech never wavered.

sentences.zh: 大統二年，詔贈龍驤將軍、巴州刺史。

translations.literal: In the second year of Datong, an edict posthumously granted Dragon Cavalry General and Inspector of Bazhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Datong, an edict posthumously appointed him Dragon Cavalry General and Inspector of Bazhou.

sentences.zh: 乙速孤佛保，北秀容胡酋也。

translations.literal: Yisu Gubao was a chieftain of the Northern Xiurong Hu.
translations.idiomatic: Yisu Gubao was a chieftain of the Northern Xiurong Hu.

sentences.zh: 少驍武，善射。

translations.literal: In youth he was valiant and martial, skilled in archery.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he was fierce in battle and an expert archer.

sentences.zh: 孝武帝時，為直閣將軍。

translations.literal: During Emperor Xiaowu's reign he served as Direct Gate General.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Xiaowu he served as Direct Gate General.

sentences.zh: 從入關，封蒲子縣公，並賜弓矢。

translations.literal: Following the entry into Guan, he was enfeoffed as Duke of Puzi County and was also granted bow and arrows.
translations.idiomatic: When the court entered the Guan region, he was enfeoffed as Duke of Puzi County and granted bow and arrows.

sentences.zh: 大統初，梁將蘭欽來寇，遂陷漢中。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Datong, the Liang general Lan Qin came to raid and thereupon captured Hanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Datong era the Liang general Lan Qin invaded and captured Hanzhong.

sentences.zh: 佛保時為都督，統兵力戰。

translations.literal: Gubao was then Area Commander and led his troops in fierce battle.
translations.idiomatic: Gubao was then area commander and led his troops in a desperate fight.

sentences.zh: 知將敗，乃先城未陷，仰天大哭曰：「此馬吾常所乘，此弓矢天恩賜我，豈可令賊得吾弓馬乎！」

translations.literal: Knowing he would be defeated, while the city had not yet fallen he looked up to heaven and wept aloud, saying: "This horse I have always ridden; these bow and arrows the Son of Heaven granted me—how can I let bandits obtain my bow and horse!
translations.idiomatic: Seeing defeat was inevitable, he wept to heaven before the city fell: "This horse I have always ridden; these bow and arrows the emperor bestowed on me—how can I let the enemy take my bow and horse!

sentences.zh: 遂斬馬及弓，自刎而死。

translations.literal: Thereupon he slew the horse and bow and cut his own throat to die.
translations.idiomatic: He slew his horse and broke his bow, then cut his own throat and died.

sentences.zh: 三軍莫不壯之。

translations.literal: Throughout the three armies none failed to find it magnificent.
translations.idiomatic: Every man in the army was stirred by his deed.

sentences.zh: 黃門郎趙僧慶時使漢中，聞，乃收運其屍致長安。

translations.literal: The Yellow Gate Gentleman Zhao Sengqing was then on mission in Hanzhong; on hearing of it he collected and transported the corpse to Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: The Yellow Gate Gentleman Zhao Sengqing was then on mission in Hanzhong; when he heard the news, he gathered the body and had it conveyed to Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 天子歎感，詔著作錄之。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven sighed in admiration and ordered the historiographical office to record it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was deeply moved and ordered the historiographers to set the account down in writing.

sentences.zh: 李棠，字長卿，勃海蓚人也。

translations.literal: Li Tang, style name Changqing, was a man of Xiurong in Bohai.
translations.idiomatic: Li Tang, courtesy name Changqing, was a native of Xiurong in Bohai.

sentences.zh: 祖伯貴，魏宣武時，官至魯郡守。

translations.literal: His grandfather Bo Gui, in the time of Emperor Xuanwu of Wei, reached the office of Administrator of Lu Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Bo Gui had risen to Administrator of Lu Commandery under Emperor Xuanwu of Wei.

sentences.zh: 有孝行，居父喪，哀戚過禮，遂以毀卒。

translations.literal: He possessed filial conduct; dwelling in mourning for his father, his grief exceeded the rites, and he thereupon died from grief-wasting.
translations.idiomatic: He was known for filial piety; during his father's mourning his grief exceeded the prescribed rites, and he died of grief.

sentences.zh: 宣武嘉之，贈勃海相。

translations.literal: Xuanwu commended him and posthumously granted Chancellor of Bohai.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuanwu praised him and posthumously appointed him Chancellor of Bohai.

sentences.zh: 父元胄，員外散騎侍郎。

translations.literal: His father Yuan Zhou was an Extraordinary Attendant Cavalier Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yuan Zhou served as Extraordinary Attendant Cavalier Attendant.

sentences.zh: 棠幼孤，好學，有志操。

translations.literal: Tang was orphaned in youth, loved learning, and possessed resolve and integrity.
translations.idiomatic: Tang lost his father young, loved learning, and was a man of firm principle.

sentences.zh: 高仲密為北豫州刺史，請棠為掾。

translations.literal: Gao Zhongmi was Inspector of Northern Yuzhou and invited Tang as his aide.
translations.idiomatic: When Gao Zhongmi became Inspector of Northern Yuzhou, he invited Tang to serve as his aide.

sentences.zh: 仲密將圖西附。

translations.literal: Zhongmi was about to plot to attach himself to the west.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongmi was planning to defect to the Western Wei.

sentences.zh: 時東魏又遣鎮城奚壽興典兵事。

translations.literal: At that time Eastern Wei also sent Xi Shouxing of Zhencheng to oversee military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Eastern Wei had meanwhile sent Xi Shouxing of Zhencheng to take charge of the garrison.

sentences.zh: 仲密遂與堂謀殺壽興，率其眾據城，遣棠詣關中歸款。

translations.literal: Zhongmi thereupon with Tang plotted to kill Shouxing, led his followers to hold the city, and sent Tang to Guanzhong to offer allegiance.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongmi then joined Li Tang in a plot to kill Xi Shouxing, seized the city with his troops, and sent Tang to Guanzhong to submit to Western Wei.

sentences.zh: 周文嘉之，封廣宗縣公，位給事黃門侍郎，加車騎大將軍、儀同三司、散騎常侍。

translations.literal: Yuwen Tai commended him, enfeoffed him as Duke of Guangzong County, appointed him Attending Affairs Yellow Gate Gentleman, and added Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry, Equal in Honor to the Three Excellencies, and Regular Attendant Cavalier Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Tai praised him, enfeoffed him as Duke of Guangzong County, and appointed him Attending Affairs Yellow Gate Gentleman, with additional titles of Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry, Equal in Honor to the Three Excellencies, and Regular Attendant Cavalier Attendant.

sentences.zh: 從魏安公尉遲迥伐蜀，棠乃應募喻之。

translations.literal: Following Duke Wei'an Chi Jue in the campaign against Shu, Tang thereupon answered the recruitment and exhorted them.
translations.idiomatic: When he followed Duke Wei'an Chi Jue on the campaign against Shu, Tang answered the call to arms and rallied the troops.

sentences.zh: 既入成都，蕭捴問迥軍中委曲，棠不對。

translations.literal: After entering Chengdu, Xiao Yan asked about the details of Jiong's army; Tang did not answer.
translations.idiomatic: After Chengdu fell, the Liang general Xiao Yan questioned him about Chi Jue's army; Tang refused to reply.

sentences.zh: 捴乃苦辱之。

translations.literal: Yan thereupon cruelly humiliated him.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Yan then subjected him to brutal humiliation.

sentences.zh: 棠曰：「我王者忠臣，有死而已，義不為爾移志也。」

translations.literal: Tang said: "I am a loyal minister of the king; I have only death—that is all—and in righteousness I will not shift my resolve for you.
translations.idiomatic: Tang said, "I am a loyal servant of my sovereign. I have only death to offer, and I will not bend my will for your sake.

sentences.zh: 遂害之。

translations.literal: They thereupon killed him.
translations.idiomatic: They killed him.

sentences.zh: 子敞嗣。

translations.literal: His son Chang inherited.
translations.idiomatic: His son Chang succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 杜叔毗，字子弼，其先京兆杜陵人也，徙居襄陽。

translations.literal: Du Shupi, style name Zibi, his ancestors were men of Duling in Jingzhao and moved to reside in Xiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: Du Shupi, courtesy name Zibi, came from a family originally of Duling in Jingzhao that had relocated to Xiangyang.

sentences.zh: 父漸，梁邊城太守。

translations.literal: His father Jian was Administrator of Biancheng under Liang.
translations.idiomatic: His father Jian had served as Administrator of Biancheng under the Liang.

sentences.zh: 叔毗早歲而孤，事母以孝聞。

translations.literal: Shupi was orphaned in early years and served his mother with a reputation for filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: Shupi lost his father young and was known throughout the region for his devotion to his mother.

sentences.zh: 仕梁，為宜豐侯蕭脩府中直兵參軍。

translations.literal: Serving Liang, he was Direct Troops Aide in the household of the Marquis of Yifeng, Xiao Xiu.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Liang he served as Direct Troops Aide in the household of Marquis Yifeng Xiao Xiu.

sentences.zh: 周文令大將軍達奚武圍脩于南鄭，脩令叔毗詣闕請和。

translations.literal: Yuwen Tai ordered the Grand General Daxi Wu to besiege Xiu at Nanzheng; Xiu ordered Shupi to go to the court to seek peace.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Tai sent Grand General Daxi Wu to besiege Xiao Xiu at Nanzheng; Xiu dispatched Shupi to the Zhou court to sue for peace.

sentences.zh: 周文見而禮之。

translations.literal: Yuwen Tai received him and treated him with courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Tai received him with honor.

sentences.zh: 使未及還，而脩中直兵曹策、參軍劉曉謀以城降武。

translations.literal: The envoy had not yet returned when Xiu's Direct Troops officer Cao Ce and Aide Liu Xiao plotted to surrender the city to Wu.
translations.idiomatic: Before Shupi could return, Xiao Xiu's Direct Troops officer Cao Ce and aide Liu Xiao plotted to hand the city over to Daxi Wu.

sentences.zh: 時叔毗兄君錫為脩中記室參軍，從子映錄事參軍，映弟晰中直兵參軍，各領部曲。

translations.literal: At that time Shupi's elder brother Junxi was Xiu's Secretariat Aide, his nephew Ying was Records Aide, Ying's younger brother Xi was Direct Troops Aide, each commanding their own followers.
translations.idiomatic: Shupi's elder brother Junxi served as Xiao Xiu's secretariat aide; his nephew Ying as records aide; Ying's younger brother Xi as direct troops aide—each commanded his own retainers.

sentences.zh: 策等忌之，懼不同己，遂誣以謀叛，擅加害焉。

translations.literal: Ce and the others envied them, fearing they would not agree with them, and thereupon falsely accused them of plotting rebellion and on their own authority added injury.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Ce and his faction feared the Du clan would not join them, falsely accused them of treason, and murdered them on their own authority.

sentences.zh: 尋討策等禽之。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward they investigated and captured Ce and the others.
translations.idiomatic: When the plot came to light, Cao Ce and his accomplices were arrested.

sentences.zh: 城降，策至長安，叔毗朝夕號泣，具申冤狀。

translations.literal: The city surrendered; Ce arrived in Chang'an; Shupi wept and wailed morning and evening, fully stating the grievance.
translations.idiomatic: After the city surrendered, Cao Ce was sent to Chang'an. Shupi wept day and night before the authorities, laying out the full account of the injustice.

sentences.zh: 朝議以事在歸附之前，不可追罪。

translations.literal: Court deliberation held that the affair occurred before submission and guilt could not be pursued.
translations.idiomatic: The court ruled that because the murders had occurred before the surrender, Cao Ce could not be punished retroactively.

sentences.zh: 叔毗志在復仇，然恐坐及其母。

translations.literal: Shupi's will was set on revenge, yet he feared implicating his mother.
translations.idiomatic: Shupi burned for revenge but feared his mother would suffer if he acted.

sentences.zh: 母曰：「汝兄橫罹禍酷，痛切骨髓。

translations.literal: His mother said: "Your brothers suffered violent calamity; the pain cuts to the marrow.
translations.idiomatic: His mother said, "Your brothers were struck down without cause. The pain cuts to the bone.

sentences.zh: 若曹策朝死，吾以夕歿，亦所甘心。

translations.literal: If Cao Ce dies in the morning, I would die in the evening—that too would be to my heart's content.
translations.idiomatic: If Cao Ce dies by morning and I die by evening, I will have no regrets.

sentences.zh: 汝何疑焉？」

translations.literal: What do you hesitate for?
translations.idiomatic: What are you waiting for?

sentences.zh: 叔毗拜受母言，後遂白日手刃策於京城，斷首瓠腹，解其支體，然後面縛請就戮焉。

translations.literal: Shupi bowed and received his mother's words; later, in broad daylight, he personally bladed Ce in the capital, severed the head and cut open the belly, dismembered the limbs, and then bound himself face-forward and requested execution.
translations.idiomatic: Shupi bowed to his mother's charge. Later, in broad daylight in the capital, he ran Cao Ce through with his own hand, cut off his head, disemboweled him, and hacked his body apart; then he bound his own hands and surrendered for execution.

sentences.zh: 周文嘉其志氣，特命舍之。

translations.literal: Yuwen Tai commended his resolve and spirit and specially ordered him spared.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Tai admired his spirit and expressly ordered him pardoned.

sentences.zh: 遭母憂，哀毀骨立，殆不勝喪。

translations.literal: He encountered mourning for his mother; his grief wasted him to bone, and he nearly could not survive the mourning.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother died, his grief wasted him to skin and bone; he nearly did not survive the mourning period.

sentences.zh: 服闋，晉公護辟為中外府樂曹參軍。

translations.literal: When mourning ended, Duke Jin Hu summoned him as Music Bureau Aide of the Central and Outer Office.
translations.idiomatic: After the mourning period, Duke Jin Yuwen Hu appointed him Music Bureau Aide of the central and outer offices.

sentences.zh: 累遷陝州刺史。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Inspector of Shanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through successive appointments to Inspector of Shanzhou.

sentences.zh: 後從衛國公直南討，軍敗，為陳人所禽。

translations.literal: Later he followed Duke Weiguo Zhi on the southern campaign; the army was defeated and he was captured by Chen men.
translations.idiomatic: Later he followed Duke Weiguo Yuwen Zhi on a southern campaign; the army was routed and Chen forces took him prisoner.

sentences.zh: 陳人將降之，叔毗辭色不撓，遂被害。

translations.literal: The Chen men were about to have him surrender; Shupi's words and bearing did not bend, and he was thereupon killed.
translations.idiomatic: The Chen offered him terms of surrender; Shupi's bearing never faltered, and they killed him.

sentences.zh: 子廉卿。

translations.literal: His son Lianqing.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Lianqing.

sentences.zh: 劉弘，字仲遠，彭城叢亭里人也。

translations.literal: Liu Hong, style name Zhongyuan, was a man of Congting Lane in Pengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Hong, courtesy name Zhongyuan, was a native of Congting Lane in Pengcheng.

sentences.zh: 少好學，有羈檢，重節概。

translations.literal: In youth he loved learning, possessed restraint, and prized integrity of principle.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he loved learning, conducted himself with discipline, and held fast to principle.

sentences.zh: 仕齊，位西楚州刺史。

translations.literal: Serving Qi, he reached the post of Inspector of Western Chuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Qi he rose to Inspector of Western Chuzhou.

sentences.zh: 齊亡，周武帝以為本郡太守。

translations.literal: When Qi perished, Emperor Wu of Zhou appointed him Administrator of his native commandery.
translations.idiomatic: After the fall of Qi, Emperor Wu of Zhou appointed him administrator of his home commandery.

sentences.zh: 及隋文帝平陳，以行車長史從總管吐萬緒度江，加上儀同，封濩澤縣公，拜泉州刺史。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen of Sui pacified Chen, as Acting Chief of Staff he followed the Commander-in-Chief Tuwan Xu across the river, was given Senior Pillar of State, enfeoffed as Duke of Huoze County, and appointed Inspector of Quanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen of Sui conquered Chen, Hong served as acting chief of staff under Commander-in-Chief Tuwan Xu for the crossing of the Yangzi. He was granted Senior Pillar of State, enfeoffed as Duke of Huoze County, and appointed Inspector of Quanzhou.

sentences.zh: 會高智慧亂，以兵攻州。

translations.literal: It happened that Gao Zhihui rebelled and led troops to attack the province.
translations.idiomatic: When Gao Zhihui rose in rebellion, his forces besieged the prefecture.

sentences.zh: 弘城守，糧盡，煮犀甲腰帶及剝樹皮食之，一無離叛。

translations.literal: Hong defended the city; when grain was exhausted they boiled rhinoceros-hide armor, belts, and stripped tree bark to eat—not one deserted.
translations.idiomatic: Hong held the city. When provisions ran out, the defenders boiled rhinoceros-hide armor and belts and stripped bark from trees to eat, yet not a single man deserted.

sentences.zh: 賊欲降之，弘抗節彌厲。

translations.literal: The bandits wished to have him surrender; Hong's defiant integrity grew ever sterner.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels pressed him to surrender; Hong's defiance only hardened.

sentences.zh: 城陷，為賊所害。

translations.literal: The city fell and he was killed by the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: When the city fell, the rebels killed him.

sentences.zh: 文帝聞而嘉歎者久之，賜物二千段。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen, on hearing of it, praised and sighed over it for a long while and granted two thousand bolts of goods.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen, on hearing the news, mourned and praised him at length, and granted two thousand bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 子長信，襲其官爵。

translations.literal: His son Changxin inherited his office and title.
translations.idiomatic: His son Changxin inherited his titles and office.

sentences.zh: 游元，字楚客，廣平任城人也。

translations.literal: You Yuan, style name Chuke, was a man of Rencheng in Guangping.
translations.idiomatic: You Yuan, courtesy name Chuke, was a native of Rencheng in Guangping.

sentences.zh: 父寶藏，位至郡守。

translations.literal: His father Baocang reached the post of commandery administrator.
translations.idiomatic: His father Baocang had risen to commandery administrator.

sentences.zh: 元少聰敏。

translations.literal: Yuan in youth was clever and keen.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan was quick-witted from childhood.

sentences.zh: 仕周，曆壽春令、譙州司馬，俱有能名。

translations.literal: Serving Zhou, he successively held the posts of Magistrate of Shouchun and Military Administrator of Qiaozhou, all with a reputation for competence.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Zhou he served as magistrate of Shouchun and military administrator of Qiaozhou, earning a reputation for ability in both posts.

sentences.zh: 開皇中，為殿內侍御史。

translations.literal: In the Kaihuang era he was Palace Attending Censor.
translations.idiomatic: During the Kaihuang era he served as palace attending censor.

sentences.zh: 煬帝嗣位，遷尚度支郎。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yang succeeded to the throne, he was transferred to Attending Master of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yang ascended the throne, Yuan was promoted to Attending Master of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 遼東之役，領左驍衛長史，為蓋牟道監軍，拜朝請大夫，兼書侍御史。

translations.literal: In the Liaodong campaign he led as Chief of Staff of the Left Valiant Cavalry Guard, served as Army Supervisor of the Gaimou Route, was appointed Grand Master for Palace Consultation, and concurrently Attending Document Censor.
translations.idiomatic: During the Liaodong campaign he served as chief of staff of the Left Valiant Cavalry Guard and army supervisor on the Gaimou Route, with concurrent appointments as Grand Master for Palace Consultation and Attending Document Censor.

sentences.zh: 宇文述等九軍敗績，帝令元主其獄。

translations.literal: Yuwen Shu and the other nine armies suffered defeat; the emperor ordered Yuan to preside over the case.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuwen Shu and eight other armies were routed, the emperor put Yuan in charge of the investigation.

sentences.zh: 述時貴幸，勢傾朝廷，遣家僮造元，有所請屬，元不之見。

translations.literal: Shu was then favored and eminent; his power tilted the court; he sent a household slave to visit Yuan with requests for favor, and Yuan did not receive him.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Shu was then the emperor's favorite and his influence dominated the court. He sent a household slave to Yuan with a private request; Yuan refused to see him.

sentences.zh: 他日，案述逾急，仍以屬請狀劾之。

translations.literal: On another day, prosecuting Shu he pressed ever harder and still used the favor-request document to impeach him.
translations.idiomatic: On another day, as the case against Yuwen Shu tightened, Yuan impeached him on the written evidence of the bribery attempt.

sentences.zh: 帝嘉其公正，賜朝服一襲。
