translations.literal: The emperor commended his impartiality and granted one suit of court robes.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised his integrity and granted him a suit of court robes.

sentences.zh: 後奉使黎陽督運。

translations.literal: Later he was sent on mission to Liyang to supervise transport.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was dispatched to Liyang to supervise grain transport.

sentences.zh: 楊玄感作逆，告以情。

translations.literal: Yang Xuangan rebelled and informed him of the situation.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Xuangan rose in rebellion, he confided his plans to Yuan.

sentences.zh: 元引正義責之，遂見困，竟不屈節，見害。

translations.literal: Yuan cited righteousness and rebuked him; he was thereupon placed in straits, yet in the end did not bend his integrity and was killed.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan rebuked him in the name of righteousness. Yang Xuangan had him seized, but Yuan never yielded and was killed.

sentences.zh: 帝甚嘉之，贈銀青光祿大夫，拜其子仁宗為正議大夫、弋陽郡通守。

translations.literal: The emperor greatly commended him, posthumously granting Silver-Gleaming Grand Master of the Palace, and appointing his son Renzong as Corrective Counselor Grand Master and General Administrator of Yiyang Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised him highly, posthumously appointing him Silver-Gleaming Grand Master of the Palace and commissioning his son Renzong as Corrective Counselor Grand Master and general administrator of Yiyang Commandery.

sentences.zh: 張須陀，弘農閿鄉人也。

translations.literal: Zhang Xuotuo was a man of Lüxiang in Hongnong.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Xuotuo was a native of Lüxiang in Hongnong.

sentences.zh: 性剛烈，有勇略。

translations.literal: By nature he was stern and fierce, possessing courage and stratagem.
translations.idiomatic: He was stern and fearless, a man of courage and cunning.

sentences.zh: 弱冠從史萬歲討西爨，以功授儀同。

translations.literal: At weak-crown age he followed Shi Wansui in the campaign against Western Cuan and for merit was granted Pillar of State.
translations.idiomatic: In his youth he followed Shi Wansui against the Western Cuan and was granted the title Pillar of State for his service.

sentences.zh: 後從楊素擊平漢王諒，加開府。

translations.literal: Later he followed Yang Su in striking down and pacifying Prince Han Liang, and was given the Open Office.
translations.idiomatic: Later he followed Yang Su in suppressing Prince Han Liang and was granted the Open Office.

sentences.zh: 大業中，為齊郡贊務。

translations.literal: In the Daye era he was Assistant Administrator of Qi Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: During the Daye era he served as assistant administrator of Qi Commandery.

sentences.zh: 會興遼東之役，歲饑，須陀將開倉賑給。

translations.literal: It happened that the Liaodong campaign was launched; the year was famine-stricken; Xuotuo was about to open the granaries for relief distribution.
translations.idiomatic: When the Liaodong campaign began, famine struck the region. Xuotuo prepared to open the granaries and distribute grain.

sentences.zh: 官屬咸曰：「須待詔敕。」

translations.literal: His subordinate officials all said: "One must await an imperial edict.
translations.idiomatic: His subordinates all said, "We must wait for an imperial edict.

sentences.zh: 須陀曰：「如待報至，當委溝壑。

translations.literal: Xuotuo said: "If we wait for the report to arrive, they will lie in ditches and ravines.
translations.idiomatic: Xuotuo replied, "If we wait for approval, the people will starve in the ditches.

sentences.zh: 吾若以此獲罪，死無所恨。」

translations.literal: If I incur guilt for this, in death I have no regret."
translations.idiomatic: If I am punished for this, I will die without regret."

sentences.zh: 先開倉而後狀，帝嘉而不責。

translations.literal: He first opened the granaries and afterward submitted his report; the emperor commended him and did not blame him.
translations.idiomatic: He opened the granaries first and reported afterward. The emperor praised him and imposed no penalty.

sentences.zh: 天下既承平日久，多不習兵。

translations.literal: The realm having long enjoyed peace, many did not practice arms.
translations.idiomatic: After generations of peace, most men in the empire had forgotten the art of war.

sentences.zh: 須陀獨勇決善戰，又長撫馭，得士卒心，號為名將。

translations.literal: Xuotuo alone was brave, resolute, and skilled in battle; he was also adept at comforting and controlling troops, winning the hearts of officers and men, and was styled a famous general.
translations.idiomatic: Xuotuo alone was bold, decisive, and skilled in battle; he knew how to win his soldiers' loyalty, and men called him a general of renown.

sentences.zh: 時賊帥王薄北連豆子<鹵亢>賊孫宣雅、石祗闍、郝孝德等，眾十餘萬，攻章丘。

translations.literal: At that time the bandit chief Wang Bo in the north linked with the Douzi bandits Sun Xuanya, Shi Zhizhan, Hao Xiaode, and others—more than a hundred thousand in all—and attacked Zhangqiu.
translations.idiomatic: The rebel leader Wang Bo joined forces in the north with the Douzi bandits Sun Xuanya, Shi Zhizhan, Hao Xiaode, and others—more than a hundred thousand strong—and attacked Zhangqiu.

sentences.zh: 須陀大破之，露布以聞。

translations.literal: Xuotuo routed them utterly and sent an unsealed victory report to inform the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Xuotuo routed them utterly and sent a victory dispatch to the capital.

sentences.zh: 帝大悅，優詔褒揚，令使者圖畫其形容奏之。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly pleased, issued a gracious edict of praise, and ordered envoys to paint his likeness and present it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was delighted, issued an edict of warm praise, and ordered envoys to paint his portrait and present it at court.

sentences.zh: 其年，賊裴長才，石子河等奄至城下，須陀與戰，長才敗走。

translations.literal: That year the bandits Pei Changcai, Shizi He, and others suddenly arrived at the city walls; Xuotuo fought them and Changcai was defeated and fled.
translations.idiomatic: That same year the rebels Pei Changcai, Shizi He, and others suddenly appeared before the city. Xuotuo gave battle and drove Changcai off in defeat.

sentences.zh: 後數旬，賊帥秦君弘、郭方預等園北海，須陀倍道而進，大敗之。

translations.literal: Several tens of days later the bandit chiefs Qin Junhong, Guo Fangyu, and others besieged Beihai; Xuotuo advanced by double marches and routed them utterly.
translations.idiomatic: Several weeks later the rebel leaders Qin Junhong and Guo Fangyu besieged Beihai. Xuotuo forced a double march and inflicted a crushing defeat.

sentences.zh: 司隸刺史裴操之上狀，帝遣使勞問之。

translations.literal: The Inspector of Sili Pei Cao submitted a report; the emperor sent envoys to comfort and inquire of him.
translations.idiomatic: Inspector of Sili Pei Cao reported the victories to the throne, and the emperor sent envoys to convey his praise.

sentences.zh: 十年，賊左孝友屯蹲狗山，須陀列八營以逼之。

translations.literal: In the tenth year the bandit Zuo Xiaoyou encamped at Dun'gou Mountain; Xuotuo arrayed eight camps to press him.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year the rebel Zuo Xiaoyou encamped on Dun'gou Mountain; Xuotuo deployed eight camps to hem him in.

sentences.zh: 孝友窘迫，面縛來降。

translations.literal: Xiaoyou was hard pressed; he came with his face bound to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Cornered, Xiaoyou came with his hands tied to surrender.

sentences.zh: 其党解象、王良、鄭大彪、李脘等眾各萬計，須陀平之，威振東夏。

translations.literal: His party members Jie Xiang, Wang Liang, Zheng Dabiao, Li Wan, and others each had forces numbering in the tens of thousands; Xuotuo pacified them, and his authority shook Eastern Xia.
translations.idiomatic: His lieutenants Jie Xiang, Wang Liang, Zheng Dabiao, Li Wan, and others each commanded forces of ten thousand or more. Xuotuo pacified them all, and his renown shook the eastern provinces.

sentences.zh: 以功遷齊郡通守，領河南道十二郡黜陟討捕大使。

translations.literal: By merit he was transferred to Defender of Qi Commandery and concurrently Grand Commissioner for Assessment, Promotion, and Demotion and Pursuit and Capture over the twelve commanderies of Henan Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: For these deeds he was promoted to Defender of Qi and named Grand Commissioner for the twelve commanderies of Henan, with authority to assess officials and pursue bandits.

sentences.zh: 俄而賊盧明月眾十餘萬將寇河北，次祝阿。

translations.literal: Before long the bandit Lu Mingyue with a host of more than a hundred thousand was about to raid Hebei and encamped at Zhu'e.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward the rebel Lu Mingyue, at the head of more than a hundred thousand men, prepared to invade Hebei and halted at Zhu'e.

sentences.zh: 須陀邀擊，殺數千人。

translations.literal: Xuotuo intercepted and struck him, killing several thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: Xuotuo intercepted him and killed several thousand.

sentences.zh: 賊呂明星、師仁泰、霍小漢等眾各萬餘，擾濟北，須陀擊走之。

translations.literal: The bandits Lü Mingxing, Shi Rentai, Huo Xiaohan, and others each had forces of more than ten thousand and harassed Jibei; Xuotuo attacked and drove them off.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels Lü Mingxing, Shi Rentai, Huo Xiaohan, and others, each with more than ten thousand men, were raiding Jibei; Xuotuo attacked and routed them.

sentences.zh: 尋將兵拒東郡賊翟讓，前後三十餘戰，每破走之。

translations.literal: He soon led troops to resist the bandits of Dong Commandery, Zhai Rang; in more than thirty engagements before and after, each time he broke and drove them off.
translations.idiomatic: He then took the field against Zhai Rang's rebels in Dong Commandery; in more than thirty battles he broke and drove them off each time.

sentences.zh: 轉榮陽通守。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Defender of Xingyang.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Defender of Xingyang.

sentences.zh: 時李密說讓取洛口倉，遂逼來滎陽。

translations.literal: At the time Li Mi urged Rang to seize the Luokou granary, and thus they pressed on toward Xingyang.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Li Mi persuaded Rang to seize the Luokou granary, and together they advanced on Xingyang.

sentences.zh: 須陀拒之，讓懼而退，須陀乘之。

translations.literal: Xuotuo resisted them; Rang feared and withdrew, and Xuotuo pursued him.
translations.idiomatic: Xuotuo held them off; Rang fled in alarm, and Xuotuo gave chase.

sentences.zh: 密先伏數千人邀擊之，須陀敗，被圍，潰輒出，左右不能盡出，復入救之，往來數四，眾皆敗。

translations.literal: Mi had first hidden several thousand men to intercept and strike him; Xuotuo was defeated and surrounded; whenever his lines broke he would break out, but his attendants could not all get out; he re-entered to rescue them, going back and forth four times, and the whole force was defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Li Mi had already hidden several thousand men to ambush him. Xuotuo was defeated and surrounded. Whenever his line broke he burst out, but not all his men could escape; he turned back four times to rescue them, until his entire force was shattered.

sentences.zh: 乃仰天曰：「兵敗如此，何面見天子乎！」

translations.literal: Then he looked up to heaven and said: "The army defeated like this—how can I have a face to see the Son of Heaven!"
translations.idiomatic: He raised his eyes to heaven and cried, "Defeated like this—what face have I left to show the emperor!

sentences.zh: 乃下馬戰死。

translations.literal: Then he dismounted and died fighting.
translations.idiomatic: With that he dismounted and fought until he was killed.

sentences.zh: 其所部兵晝夜號哭，數日不止。

translations.literal: The troops under his command wailed day and night for several days without stopping.
translations.idiomatic: His men wailed day and night for many days without cease.

sentences.zh: 帝令其子元備總父兵。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered his son Yuanbei to take overall command of his father's army.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered his son Yuanbei to take command of his father's troops.

sentences.zh: 元備時在齊郡，遇賊，竟不果行。

translations.literal: Yuanbei was at the time in Qi Commandery; he encountered bandits and in the end did not succeed in setting out.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanbei was then in Qi Commandery; he met bandits on the road and never reached his post.

sentences.zh: 楊善會，字敬仁，弘農華陰人也。

translations.literal: Yang Shanhui, styled Jingren, was a man of Huayin in Hongnong.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Shanhui, styled Jingren, was a native of Huayin in Hongnong.

sentences.zh: 父初，位毗陵太守。

translations.literal: His father Chu held the post of Governor of Piling.
translations.idiomatic: His father Chu had served as Governor of Piling.

sentences.zh: 善會大業中為鄃令，以清正聞。

translations.literal: During the Daye era Shanhui served as magistrate of Shuxian and was known for integrity.
translations.idiomatic: During the Daye reign Shanhui served as magistrate of Shuxian and was known for his integrity.

sentences.zh: 俄而百姓聚起為盜，善會討之，往皆克捷。

translations.literal: Before long the common people gathered and rose as bandits; Shanhui attacked them and on each expedition achieved victory.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the people rose in bands; Shanhui attacked them and won every engagement.

sentences.zh: 後賊帥張金稱屯於縣界，善會每挫其鋒。

translations.literal: Later the bandit chief Zhang Jinheng encamped on the county border; Shanhui every time blunted his edge.
translations.idiomatic: Later the rebel chief Zhang Jinheng encamped on the county border; Shanhui repelled him at every clash.

sentences.zh: 煬帝遣將軍段達討金稱，善會進計于達，達不能用，軍竟敗。

translations.literal: Emperor Yang dispatched the general Duan Da to attack Jinheng; Shanhui presented plans to Da, but Da could not employ them, and the army in the end was defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yang sent the general Duan Da against Jinheng. Shanhui offered Da his counsel, but Da would not heed it, and the army was defeated.

sentences.zh: 後進止一以謀之，乃大克。

translations.literal: Later, in all advance and halt he relied solely on Shanhui's counsel, and then achieved great victory.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter Da followed Shanhui's advice in every move and won a great victory.

sentences.zh: 金稱復引勃海賊孫宣雅、高士雅等破黎陽而還，善會邀破之。

translations.literal: Jinheng again led the Bohai bandits Sun Xuanya, Gao Shiya, and others, broke Liyang, and returned; Shanhui intercepted and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: Jinheng again brought the Bohai rebels Sun Xuanya and Gao Shiya, stormed Liyang, and was returning when Shanhui intercepted and routed him.

sentences.zh: 擢拜朝請大夫，清河郡丞。

translations.literal: He was promoted and appointed Supervising Secretary and Assistant Governor of Qinghe Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Supervising Secretary and Assistant Governor of Qinghe.

sentences.zh: 于時山東郡縣，陷沒相繼，能抗賊者，唯善會而已。

translations.literal: At that time the commanderies and counties east of the mountains fell one after another; the only one who could resist the bandits was Shanhui alone.
translations.idiomatic: By then commandery after commandery east of the mountains had fallen; Shanhui alone still held the rebels at bay.

sentences.zh: 前後七百餘陣，未嘗負敗。

translations.literal: In more than seven hundred engagements before and after, he never once suffered defeat.
translations.idiomatic: In more than seven hundred battles he was never once defeated.

sentences.zh: 會太僕楊義臣討金稱見敗，取善會定策，與金稱戰，賊乃退走。

translations.literal: When Minister of Imperial Studs Yang Yichen attacked Jinheng and was defeated, he took Shanhui's plan; fighting Jinheng, the bandits then retreated and fled.
translations.idiomatic: When Minister of Imperial Studs Yang Yichen attacked Jinheng and was beaten, he adopted Shanhui's plan; in battle with Jinheng the rebels were driven off.

sentences.zh: 善會捕斬之，傳首行在所。

translations.literal: Shanhui captured and beheaded him and sent the head to the traveling palace.
translations.idiomatic: Shanhui captured and beheaded him and sent the head to the emperor's camp.

sentences.zh: 帝賜以尚方甲槊弓劍，進拜清河通守。

translations.literal: The emperor bestowed upon him armor, halberd, bow, and sword from the Imperial Workshop and promoted him to Defender of Qinghe.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor gave him armor, halberd, bow, and sword from the Imperial Workshop and promoted him to Defender of Qinghe.

sentences.zh: 復從楊義臣斬漳南賊帥高士達，傳首江都宮。

translations.literal: He again followed Yang Yichen in beheading the Zhangnan bandit chief Gao Shida and sent the head to the Jiangdu Palace.
translations.idiomatic: He again followed Yang Yichen in slaying the Zhangnan rebel chief Gao Shida and sent the head to the Jiangdu Palace.

sentences.zh: 帝下詔褒揚之。

translations.literal: The emperor issued an edict praising him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor issued an edict commending him.

sentences.zh: 後為竇建德所陷。

translations.literal: Later he was captured by Dou Jiande.
translations.idiomatic: Later he fell into the hands of Dou Jiande.

sentences.zh: 建德釋而禮之，用為貝州刺史。

translations.literal: Jiande released him and treated him with courtesy, employing him as Governor of Beizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Jiande released him and treated him with honor, appointing him Governor of Beizhou.

sentences.zh: 善會肆罵，臨之以兵，辭氣不撓，乃害之。

translations.literal: Shanhui cursed him with abandon; though troops were leveled at him, his words and spirit did not bend, and Jiande killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Shanhui reviled him without restraint; though weapons were trained on him, his tone never wavered, and Jiande put him to death.

sentences.zh: 清河士庶，莫不傷痛。

translations.literal: The gentry and common folk of Qinghe were all grieved.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Qinghe, high and low alike, mourned him.

sentences.zh: 盧楚，涿郡范陽人也。

translations.literal: Lu Chu was a man of Fanyang in Zhuo Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Chu was a native of Fanyang in Zhuo Commandery.

sentences.zh: 祖景祚，魏司空掾。

translations.literal: His grandfather Jingzuo was an aide in the Northern Wei Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Jingzuo had been an aide in the Wei Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 楚少有才學，性鯁急，口秘，言語澀難。

translations.literal: Chu in his youth had talent and learning; he was blunt and urgent in character, tight-lipped, and his speech was halting and difficult.
translations.idiomatic: In youth Chu was gifted and learned, but blunt and impatient, sparing of words, and awkward in speech.

sentences.zh: 大業中，為尚書左司郎。

translations.literal: During the Daye era he served as Left Bureau Director in the Ministry of State.
translations.idiomatic: During the Daye reign he served as Left Bureau Director in the Ministry of State.

sentences.zh: 當朝正色，甚為公卿所憚。

translations.literal: At court he maintained a stern countenance and was greatly feared by the grandees.
translations.idiomatic: At court he kept a stern bearing, and the high ministers feared him.

sentences.zh: 及帝幸江都，東都官僚多不奉法。

translations.literal: When the emperor traveled to Jiangdu, the officials of the Eastern Capital for the most part did not obey the law.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor went south to Jiangdu, most officials at the Eastern Capital ignored the law.

sentences.zh: 楚每存糾舉，無所回避。

translations.literal: Chu on every occasion sought to investigate and impeach, shirking nothing.
translations.idiomatic: Chu investigated and impeached without fear or favor.

sentences.zh: 越王侗稱尊號，以楚為內史令、左備身將軍、尚書左丞、右光祿大夫，封涿郡公，與元文都等同心戮力以輔侗。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Yue Yang Tong assumed the imperial title, Chu was made Grand Secretary, General of the Left Guard Reserve, Left Vice Minister of State, Right Grand Master for Splendid Happiness, enfeoffed as Duke of Zhuo Commandery, and together with Yuan Wendu and others united hearts and joined strength to assist Tong.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Yue Yang Tong took the imperial title, Chu was made Grand Secretary, General of the Left Guard Reserve, Left Vice Minister of State, and Right Grand Master for Splendid Happiness, enfeoffed as Duke of Zhuo, and with Yuan Wendu and others gave his full strength to support Tong.

sentences.zh: 及王世充作亂，兵犯太陽門。

translations.literal: When Wang Shichong made rebellion, his troops assaulted the Taiyang Gate.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Shichong rebelled, his troops attacked the Taiyang Gate.

sentences.zh: 武衛將軍皇甫無逸斬關逃難，呼楚同去。

translations.literal: Martial Guard General Huangfu Wuyi cut through the gate and fled in distress, calling Chu to go with him.
translations.idiomatic: Martial Guard General Huangfu Wuyi broke through the gate and fled, urging Chu to come with him.

sentences.zh: 楚曰：「僕與元公有約，若社稷有難，誓以俱死。

translations.literal: Chu said: "Your servant and Duke Yuan made a covenant that if the altars of state were in peril, we would swear to die together.
translations.idiomatic: Chu said, "I and Duke Yuan pledged that if the realm were in peril we would die together.

sentences.zh: 今舍去不義。」

translations.literal: To leave now would be unjust."
translations.idiomatic: To flee now would be faithless.

sentences.zh: 及世充入，楚匿太官署，執之。

translations.literal: When Shichong entered, Chu hid in the Imperial Provisioner's office and was seized.
translations.idiomatic: When Shichong entered the city, Chu hid in the Imperial Provisioner's office and was taken.

sentences.zh: 世充奮袂令斬，於是鋒刃交下，支體糜碎。

translations.literal: Shichong jerked his sleeve and ordered him beheaded; then blades crossed and his limbs were shredded to pulp.
translations.idiomatic: Shichong swept his sleeve and ordered him cut down; blades fell from every side until his body was torn to pieces.

sentences.zh: 劉子翊，彭城叢亭里人也。

translations.literal: Liu Ziyi was a man of Congting Lane in Pengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Ziyi was a native of Congting Lane in Pengcheng.

sentences.zh: 父遍，齊徐州司馬。

translations.literal: His father Bian was Si Ma of Xuzhou in Qi.
translations.idiomatic: His father Bian had been Sima of Xuzhou under Qi.

sentences.zh: 子翊少好學，頗解屬文。

translations.literal: Ziyi in his youth loved learning and was quite able in literary composition.
translations.idiomatic: Ziyi loved learning from youth and was skilled at composition.

sentences.zh: 性剛謇，有吏幹。

translations.literal: His nature was stern and upright; he had administrative ability.
translations.idiomatic: He was stern and upright by nature and capable in office.

sentences.zh: 開皇中，為秦州司法參軍。

translations.literal: During the Kaihuang era he served as Judicial Assistant of Qin Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: During the Kaihuang reign he served as Judicial Assistant in Qin Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 因入考，楊素奏為侍御史。

translations.literal: Because he entered for evaluation, Yang Su memorialized making him Attending Censor.
translations.idiomatic: When he came to the capital for review, Yang Su recommended him as Attending Censor.

sentences.zh: 時永甯縣令李公孝，四歲喪母，九歲外繼。

translations.literal: At the time the magistrate of Yongning, Li Gongxiao, at age four lost his mother and at age nine was adopted out.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Li Gongxiao, magistrate of Yongning, had lost his mother at four and been given in adoption at nine.

sentences.zh: 其後，父更別娶後妻，至是而亡。

translations.literal: Afterward his father took another wife in addition, and she now died.
translations.idiomatic: Later his father had taken another wife, and she now died.

sentences.zh: 河間劉炫以為無撫育之恩，議不解任。

translations.literal: Liu Xuan of Hejian held that there had been no nurturing affection and argued he need not leave office.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xuan of Hejian held that Gongxiao owed her no rearing and argued he need not leave office.

sentences.zh: 子翊駁之曰：

translations.literal: Ziyi refuted him, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Ziyi rebutted him:

sentences.zh: 《傳》云：「繼母，同母也。」

translations.literal: The Commentary says: "A stepmother—same as a mother.
translations.idiomatic: The Commentary says, "A stepmother is the same as a mother.

sentences.zh: 當以配父之尊，居母之位，齊杖之制，皆如親母。

translations.literal: She should be matched to the father's honor, occupy the mother's station; the regulations for one-year mourning staff—all like a birth mother.
translations.idiomatic: She is joined to the father's dignity and holds the mother's place; the rules of one-year mourning with staff are the same as for a birth mother.

sentences.zh: 又「為人後者為其父母期」，服者，自以本生，非殊親之與繼也。

translations.literal: Also, "One who becomes an heir observes one-year mourning for his parents"; the one who wears mourning does so by reason of birth, not because the relationship with an adoptive parent differs from that with a stepmother.
translations.idiomatic: Again, "One who becomes an heir wears one-year mourning for his parents"; the mourner does so by birth tie, not because adoptive kin differs from a stepmother.

sentences.zh: 父雖自處傍尊之地，於子之情，猶須隆其本重。

translations.literal: Though the father may place himself in the position of collateral honor, toward the son's feelings one must still exalt the weight of the birth tie.
translations.idiomatic: Though the father stands in a secondary rank, the son's feelings must still honor the weight of his birth parents.

sentences.zh: 是以令云：「為人後者，其父母，並解官申其心喪。

translations.literal: Hence the ordinance says: "One who becomes an heir—for his parents, both are to leave office and declare inner mourning.
translations.idiomatic: Hence the ordinance: "One who becomes an heir must leave office for both parents and observe inner mourning.

sentences.zh: 父卒母嫁，為父後者雖不服，亦申心喪；

translations.literal: If the father dies and the mother remarries, one who becomes father's heir, though not wearing mourning garb, still declares inner mourning;
translations.idiomatic: If the father dies and the mother remarries, the heir, though not in mourning dress, still observes inner mourning;

sentences.zh: 其繼母嫁，不解官。」

translations.literal: when the stepmother remarries, he does not leave office.
translations.idiomatic: when the stepmother remarries, he does not leave office.

sentences.zh: 此專據嫁者生文耳。

translations.literal: This applies solely to the text generated by the mother's remarriage.
translations.idiomatic: That passage speaks only of remarriage.

sentences.zh: 將知繼母在父之室，則制同親母。

translations.literal: One may know that when the stepmother is in the father's household, the regulations are the same as for a birth mother.
translations.idiomatic: It follows that while the stepmother remains in the father's house, the rites are the same as for a birth mother.

sentences.zh: 若謂非有撫育之恩，同之行路，何服之有乎？

translations.literal: If one says there was no nurturing affection and she is the same as someone met on the road, what mourning would there be?
translations.idiomatic: If one claims there was no rearing and she is no more than a stranger on the road, what mourning could there be?

sentences.zh: 服既有之，心喪焉可獨異？

translations.literal: If mourning garb exists, how can inner mourning alone differ?
translations.idiomatic: If formal mourning exists, how can inner mourning alone be different?

sentences.zh: 三省令旨，其義甚明。

translations.literal: The intent of the ordinance from the Three Ministries is very clear.
translations.idiomatic: The intent of the ordinance from the Three Ministries is perfectly clear.

sentences.zh: 今言令許不解，何其甚謬？

translations.literal: Now to say the ordinance permits not leaving office—how extremely mistaken!
translations.idiomatic: To claim the ordinance allows one to stay in office—how far wrong can one be?

sentences.zh: 且後人者為其父母期，未有變隔以親繼，親既等，故心喪不得有殊。

translations.literal: Moreover, one who becomes an heir observes one-year mourning for his parents; there is no changing or separating the birth and adoptive ties; since the kinship is equal, inner mourning must not differ.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, an heir wears one-year mourning for his parents; birth and adoptive ties are not split apart; kinship being equal, inner mourning cannot differ.

sentences.zh: 《服問》云：「母出，則為繼母之党服。」

translations.literal: Questions on Mourning Garb says: "When the mother leaves, one wears mourning for the stepmother's kin.
translations.idiomatic: Questions on Mourning says, "When the mother departs, one mourns the stepmother's kin.

sentences.zh: 豈不以出母族絕，推而遠之；

translations.literal: Is it not because the birth mother's lineage is severed and one pushes them away afar;
translations.idiomatic: Is this not because the birth mother's line is cut off and pushed away;

sentences.zh: 繼母配父，引而親之乎？

translations.literal: whereas the stepmother is matched to the father and drawn near as kin?
translations.idiomatic: while the stepmother is joined to the father and drawn near as kin?

sentences.zh: 子思曰：「為伋也妻，是為白也母；

translations.literal: Zisi said: "Taking a wife for Ji makes her Bai's mother;
translations.idiomatic: Zisi said, "Taking a wife for Ji makes her Bai's mother;

sentences.zh: 不為伋也妻，是不為白也母。」

translations.literal: not taking a wife for Ji means she is not Bai's mother.
translations.idiomatic: not taking a wife for Ji means she is not Bai's mother.

sentences.zh: 定知服以名重，情以父親。

translations.literal: This establishes that mourning garb follows the weight of the name, affection follows the father's kinship.
translations.idiomatic: This shows that mourning follows the weight of the name, affection follows the father's bond.

sentences.zh: 所以聖人敦之以孝慈，弘之以名義。

translations.literal: Therefore the sages deepened this with filial kindness and enlarged it with righteous repute.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore the sages strengthened it through filial kindness and spread it through righteous name.

sentences.zh: 是使子以名服，同之親母；

translations.literal: Thus the son wears mourning by the name, the same as for a birth mother;
translations.idiomatic: Thus the son mourns by the name, the same as for a birth mother;

sentences.zh: 繼母以義報，等之己生。

translations.literal: the stepmother reciprocates by righteous obligation, equal to what she bore herself.
translations.idiomatic: the stepmother repays by righteous duty, equal to what she bore herself.

sentences.zh: 論云：「禮者稱情而立文，杖義而設教。」

translations.literal: The Discourses say: "Rites weigh feeling to establish pattern, uphold righteousness to set teaching.
translations.idiomatic: The Discourses say, "Rites weigh feeling to establish form and uphold righteousness to set teaching.

sentences.zh: 還以此義，諭彼之情。

translations.literal: Applying this principle to explain that situation.
translations.idiomatic: Apply this principle to that case.

sentences.zh: 稱情者如母之情，杖義者為子之義。

translations.literal: "Weighing feeling" means like a mother's feeling; "upholding righteousness" means as a son's righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: "Weighing feeling" means a mother's feeling; "upholding righteousness" means a son's duty.

sentences.zh: 分定然後能尊父順名，崇禮篤敬。

translations.literal: Only when roles are fixed can one honor the father and follow the name, esteem rites and deepen reverence.
translations.idiomatic: Only when roles are fixed can one honor the father, follow the name, esteem rites, and deepen reverence.

sentences.zh: 苟以姆養之恩，始成母子。

translations.literal: If one holds that nursemaid rearing affection first formed the mother-son bond,
translations.idiomatic: If one holds that a nurse's rearing first made mother and son,

sentences.zh: 則恩由彼至，服自己來。

translations.literal: then affection came from her, mourning garb from oneself.
translations.idiomatic: then affection came from her and mourning from oneself.

sentences.zh: 則慈母如母，何待父令？

translations.literal: then the nourishing mother is like a mother—why wait for the father's command?
translations.idiomatic: Then the nourishing mother would be like a mother—why wait for the father's order?

sentences.zh: 又云：「繼母、慈母，本實路人，臨己養己，同之骨血。」

translations.literal: It also says: "Stepmother and nourishing mother were originally strangers on the road; facing one they raised, they are kin like bone and blood.
translations.idiomatic: It also says, "Stepmother and nourishing mother were strangers at first; when they came to raise you, they became kin like bone and blood.

sentences.zh: 基如斯言，子不由父，縱有恩育，得如母乎？

translations.literal: Based on such words, the son does not act by the father's order; though there is nurturing kindness, can it be like a mother?
translations.idiomatic: On such grounds, the son does not act by the father's command; however much rearing there was, could it equal a mother?

sentences.zh: 其慈繼雖在三年之下，而居齊期之上。

translations.literal: For nourishing and step mothers, though below the three-year grade, they rank above one-year mourning.
translations.idiomatic: For nourishing and step mothers, though below three-year mourning, they stand above one-year mourning.

sentences.zh: 禮有倫例，服以稱情。

translations.literal: Rites have orderly examples; mourning garb weighs feeling.
translations.idiomatic: Rites have their order; mourning weighs feeling.

sentences.zh: 繼母本以名服，豈藉恩之厚薄也。

translations.literal: A stepmother's mourning originally follows the name; how can it depend on the thickness or thinness of affection?
translations.idiomatic: A stepmother's mourning follows the name, not the depth of affection.

sentences.zh: 至於兄弟之子猶子也，私昵之心實殊，禮服之制無二。

translations.literal: As for a brother's son, he is like a son; private fondness in the heart truly differs, yet the pattern of mourning garb is not doubled.
translations.idiomatic: A brother's son is like one's own son; private feeling may differ, yet the mourning rites do not.

sentences.zh: 彼言「以」輕「如」重，因以不同；

translations.literal: That saying uses "light" for "like" heavy—thus making them different;
translations.idiomatic: They take "light" for "like" heavy and so make them different;

sentences.zh: 此謂如重之辭，即同重法。

translations.literal: this says the word "like" heavy means it follows the law of full heavy mourning.
translations.idiomatic: this holds that the word "like" heavy means the law of full heavy mourning.

sentences.zh: 若使輕重不等，何得為「如」？

translations.literal: If light and heavy were not equal, how could one use "like"?
translations.idiomatic: If light and heavy were unequal, how could one say "like"?

sentences.zh: 律云「准枉法」者，但准其罪，「以枉法論」者，即同真法。

translations.literal: The code says "comparable to bending the law"—only comparable in guilt; "treated as bending the law"—then it is the same as true law-breaking.
translations.idiomatic: The code says "comparable to bending the law" counts only as comparable guilt; "treated as bending the law" is the same as true violation.

sentences.zh: 律以弊刑，禮以設教。

translations.literal: The code uses penal correction; rites use establishing teaching.
translations.idiomatic: The code employs penal correction; rites establish moral teaching.

sentences.zh: 「准」者准擬之名，「以」者即真之稱。

translations.literal: "Comparable" is the name for comparison; "treated as" is the designation for what is truly so.
translations.idiomatic: "Comparable" names a likeness; "treated as" designates the genuine case.

sentences.zh: 「如」、「以」二字，義用不殊，禮、律兩文，所防是一。

translations.literal: The two words "like" and "treated as" differ not in meaning and use; rites and code, two texts, guard against the same thing.
translations.idiomatic: The words "like" and "treated as" share the same meaning and use; the rites and the code alike guard one principle.

sentences.zh: 將此明彼，足見其義。

translations.literal: Using this to clarify that fully shows its meaning.
translations.idiomatic: Apply this to that case and the principle is plain.

sentences.zh: 取譬伐柯，何遠之有。

translations.literal: Take the analogy of felling a handle—what distance is there?
translations.idiomatic: Like felling a handle by its model—the parallel is close at hand.

sentences.zh: 論云：「取子為後者，將以供承祧廟，奉養己身。

translations.literal: The Discourses say: "One who takes a son as heir does so to supply succession to the ancestral temple and to support one's own person.
translations.idiomatic: The Discourses say, "One who adopts a son as heir does so to maintain the ancestral line and support oneself.

sentences.zh: 不得使宗子歸其故宅，以子道事本父之後妻也。」

translations.literal: One must not let the heir by descent return to his former house, or serve the birth father's later wife in the way of a son.
translations.idiomatic: One must not let the heir return to his former home or treat the birth father's later wife as a son would.

sentences.zh: 然本父後妻，因父而得母稱。

translations.literal: Yet the birth father's later wife gains the title of mother through the father.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the birth father's later wife is called mother through the father's bond.

sentences.zh: 若如來旨，本父亦可無心喪乎？

translations.literal: If one follows your position, can the birth father also be without inner mourning?
translations.idiomatic: By your reasoning, could one also omit inner mourning for the birth father?

sentences.zh: 何直父之後妻也。

translations.literal: Why only the father's later wife?
translations.idiomatic: Why single out only the father's later wife?

sentences.zh: 論又云：「《禮》言舊君，其尊豈後君乎？

translations.literal: The Discourses further say: "The Rites speak of the former lord—is his honor not below the later lord?
translations.idiomatic: The Discourses also say, "The Rites speak of the 'former lord'—is his dignity not below the present lord?

sentences.zh: 已去其位，非復純臣，須言'舊'以殊之。

translations.literal: Having left his post, he is no longer a pure minister; one must say 'former' to distinguish him.
translations.idiomatic: Having left office, he is no longer a loyal subject in full; one says 'former' to mark the change.

sentences.zh: 別有所重，非復純孝，故言'其'已見之，目以'其父'之文，是名異也。」

translations.literal: A different weight applies, not pure filial piety; hence one says 'his' when already in view, designated by the text 'his father'—that is a difference in name.
translations.idiomatic: A different weight applies—not pure filial piety—hence 'his' when already in view, designated by the text 'his father'; that is a difference in name.

sentences.zh: 此又非通論。

translations.literal: This is again not sound doctrine.
translations.idiomatic: This too is unsound doctrine.

sentences.zh: 何以言之？

translations.literal: How so?
translations.idiomatic: On what grounds?

sentences.zh: 「其」「舊」訓殊，所用亦別。

translations.literal: "His" and "former" differ in gloss; their uses are also distinct.
translations.idiomatic: "His" and "former" differ in meaning; their uses are also distinct.

sentences.zh: 「舊」者易新之稱，「其」者因彼之辭，安得以相類哉？

translations.literal: "Former" is what replaces "new"; "his" is a word that follows from the other—how can they be classed together?
translations.idiomatic: "Former" marks what replaces the new; "his" is a word that follows from the other—how can they be classed together?

sentences.zh: 至如《禮》云：「其父析薪，其子不克負荷。」

translations.literal: As for the Rites, it says: "His father split firewood; his son cannot bear the load.
translations.idiomatic: As the Rites say, "His father split firewood; his son cannot bear the load.

sentences.zh: 《傳》云：「衛雖小，其君在焉。」

translations.literal: The Commentary says: "Though Wei is small, its lord is there.
translations.idiomatic: The Commentary says, "Though Wei is small, its lord is there.

sentences.zh: 若其父而有異，其君復有異乎？

translations.literal: If "his father" carries a special sense, does "its lord" likewise?
translations.idiomatic: If "his father" carries a special sense, does "its lord" as well?

sentences.zh: 斯不然矣。

translations.literal: That is not so.
translations.idiomatic: That cannot be so.

sentences.zh: 今炫敢違禮乖令，侮聖幹法，使出後之子，無情於本生，名義之分，有虧於風俗，徇飾非於明世，強媒蘖於《禮經》，雖欲揚己露才，不覺言之傷理。

translations.literal: Now Xuan dares violate rites and resist ordinances, insult the sages and impugn the law, causing sons who became heirs to be without feeling toward their birth kin—the division of name and righteousness is damaged in custom; he indulges false display in an enlightened age and forcibly breeds scandal against the Book of Rites; though he would exalt himself and show talent, he does not perceive his words injure principle.
translations.idiomatic: Now Xuan dares defy rites and resist the law, insult the sages and impugn statute, so that adopted sons feel nothing for their birth kin—the bond of name and righteousness is harmed in custom; he panders to error in an enlightened age and forcibly slanders the Book of Rites; though he would exalt himself and display talent, he does not see that his words violate reason.

sentences.zh: 事奏，竟從子翊之議。

translations.literal: The matter was submitted; in the end they followed Ziyi's proposal.
translations.idiomatic: When the case was reported, the court in the end adopted Ziyi's view.

sentences.zh: 曆新豐令、大理正，並有能名。

translations.literal: He served successively as magistrate of Xinfeng and senior corrector at the Court of Judicial Review, and in both posts had a reputation for competence.
translations.idiomatic: He served as magistrate of Xinfeng and senior corrector at the Court of Judicial Review, winning a reputation for ability in both posts.

sentences.zh: 擢授書侍御史。

translations.literal: He was promoted and appointed supervising secretary in the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to supervising secretary in the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 每朝廷疑議，子翊為之辯析，多出眾人意表。

translations.literal: Whenever the court had doubtful cases, Ziyi argued and analyzed them, often going beyond what others expected.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the court faced doubtful cases, Ziyi argued them through, often exceeding what others had foreseen.

sentences.zh: 從幸江東。

translations.literal: He accompanied the emperor on the tour to Jiangdong.
translations.idiomatic: He accompanied the emperor on the Jiangdong tour.

sentences.zh: 屬天下大亂，帝猶不悟。

translations.literal: Just then the realm fell into great disorder, yet the emperor still did not see it.
translations.idiomatic: The realm was falling into chaos, yet the emperor still would not see it.

sentences.zh: 子翊因侍切諫，由是忤旨，令子翊為丹陽留守。

translations.literal: Ziyi remonstrated sharply while in attendance; thereby he offended the throne and was ordered to serve as regent of Danyang.
translations.idiomatic: Ziyi remonstrated sharply in attendance; thereby he offended the throne and was made regent of Danyang.

sentences.zh: 尋遣於上江督運，為賊吳棋子所虜。

translations.literal: Soon he was sent to supervise transport on the Upper Yangtze and was captured by the bandit Wu Qizi.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was sent to oversee transport on the upper Yangtze and was captured by the bandit Wu Qizi.

sentences.zh: 子翊說之，因以眾降。

translations.literal: Ziyi persuaded him, and thereby the whole force surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Ziyi persuaded him, and the whole band surrendered.

sentences.zh: 復遣首領賊渡江，遇煬帝被殺，知而告之。

translations.literal: He again sent bandit chiefs across the river; they encountered that Emperor Yang had been killed and told him.
translations.idiomatic: He again sent bandit leaders across the river; they learned Emperor Yang had been killed and reported it.

sentences.zh: 子翊弗信，斬所言者。

translations.literal: Ziyi did not believe it and beheaded those who spoke.
translations.idiomatic: Ziyi refused to believe it and executed the messengers.

sentences.zh: 賊又請以為主，不從。

translations.literal: The bandits again asked to make him their leader; he would not consent.
translations.idiomatic: The bandits again asked to make him their chief; he would not agree.

sentences.zh: 因執至臨川城下，使告城中云「帝崩」。

translations.literal: They then seized him to the foot of Linchuan city wall and made him announce to the city that "the emperor is dead."
translations.idiomatic: They then took him to the foot of Linchuan's walls and made him tell the city, "The emperor is dead."

sentences.zh: 子翊乃易其言，於是見害。

translations.literal: Ziyi then changed the words of the message; thereupon he was killed.
translations.idiomatic: Ziyi altered the message; thereupon he was killed.

sentences.zh: 堯君素，魏郡湯陰人也。

translations.literal: Yao Junsu was a man of Tangyin in Wei Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Junsu was a native of Tangyin in Wei Commandery.

sentences.zh: 煬帝為晉王時，君素為左右。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yang was Prince of Jin, Junsu was in his personal staff.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yang was Prince of Jin, Junsu served in his personal entourage.

sentences.zh: 帝嗣位，累遷鷹揚郎將。

translations.literal: When the emperor succeeded to the throne, Junsu was repeatedly promoted to Eagle-Flying Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: After the emperor took the throne, Junsu rose repeatedly to Eagle-Flying Commandant.

sentences.zh: 大業末，從驍衛大將軍屈突通拒義師於河東。

translations.literal: At the end of the Daye era he followed the brave-guard grand general Qu Tuotong in resisting the righteous army at Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Daye era he followed Valiant Guard Commander-in-Chief Qu Tuotong in holding Hedong against the righteous army.

sentences.zh: 俄而通引兵南遁，置君素領河東通守。

translations.literal: Before long Tuotong led the army south in flight and left Junsu in charge as defender of Hedong communications.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Tuotong fled south with his army and left Junsu as defender of Hedong communications.

sentences.zh: 義師遣將呂紹宗、韋義節等攻之不克。

translations.literal: The righteous army sent generals Lü Shaozong, Wei Yijie, and others to attack but could not overcome him.
translations.idiomatic: The righteous army sent generals Lü Shaozong, Wei Yijie, and others against him but could not take the city.

sentences.zh: 及通軍敗，至城下呼之。

translations.literal: When Tuotong's army was defeated, he came to the city wall and called to him.
translations.idiomatic: When Tuotong's army was beaten, he came to the walls and called out to him.

sentences.zh: 君素見通，歔欷流涕，悲不自勝，左右皆哽咽。

translations.literal: Junsu saw Tuotong; he sobbed and wept, grief beyond bearing, and those at his side all choked with tears.
translations.idiomatic: Junsu saw Tuotong and sobbed until grief overwhelmed him; all at his side choked with tears.

sentences.zh: 通亦泣下沾襟，因說君素早降以取富貴。

translations.literal: Tuotong also wept until his collar was wet and urged Junsu to surrender early and win wealth and honor.
translations.idiomatic: Tuotong wept until his collar was soaked and urged Junsu to surrender early and win rank and riches.

sentences.zh: 君素以名義責之曰：「公縱不能遠慚主上，公所乘馬，即代王所賜也，公何面目乘之哉！」

translations.literal: Junsu charged him on righteousness and reputation, saying: "Though you could not long feel shame before the sovereign, the horse you ride is the very one the Prince of Dai bestowed—what face have you to ride it!
translations.idiomatic: Junsu rebuked him on righteousness and honor: "Even if you cannot long feel shame before the sovereign, the horse you ride is the very one the Prince of Dai gave you—what face have you to mount it!

sentences.zh: 通曰：「籲！

translations.literal: Tuotong said: "Alas!
translations.idiomatic: Tuotong said, "Alas!

sentences.zh: 君素！

translations.literal: Junsu!
translations.idiomatic: Junsu!

sentences.zh: 我力屈而來。」

translations.literal: I came because my strength failed.
translations.idiomatic: I came because my strength gave out.

sentences.zh: 君素曰：「方今力猶未屈，何用多言！」

translations.literal: Junsu said: "Our strength is not yet spent—what use more words!"
translations.idiomatic: Junsu said, "Our strength is not yet spent—why say more!"

sentences.zh: 通慚而退。

translations.literal: Tuotong withdrew in shame.
translations.idiomatic: Tuotong withdrew, ashamed.

sentences.zh: 時圍甚急，行李斷絕。

translations.literal: At the time the siege was very pressing and supplies were cut off.
translations.idiomatic: The siege was fierce and supplies were cut off.

sentences.zh: 君素乃為木鵝，置表於頸，具論事勢，浮之黃河，沿流而下。

translations.literal: Junsu then made wooden geese, placed a report at the neck detailing the situation, floated them on the Yellow River, and let them drift downstream.
translations.idiomatic: Junsu then made wooden geese, tied a report at the neck describing the situation, and floated them down the Yellow River.

sentences.zh: 河陽守者得之，達於東都。

translations.literal: The defenders at Heyang retrieved one and it reached the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: The garrison at Heyang recovered one and it reached the Eastern Capital.

sentences.zh: 越王侗見而歎息，乃承制拜君素為金紫光祿大夫，密遣行人勞之。

translations.literal: Prince of Yue Tong saw it and sighed; he then issued an order on imperial authority appointing Junsu as Grand Bearer of the Golden Purple and secretly dispatched envoys to comfort him.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Yue Tong read it and sighed; he then issued an order in the emperor's name appointing Junsu Grand Bearer of the Golden Purple and secretly sent envoys to encourage him.

sentences.zh: 監門直閣龐玉、武衛將軍皇甫無逸前後自東都歸義，俱造城下，為陳利害。

translations.literal: The gate custodian attendant-director Pang Yu and martial guard general Huangfu Wuyi, before and after, came from the Eastern Capital to offer allegiance; both went to the city wall to explain advantage and harm.
translations.idiomatic: Gate custodian attendant-director Pang Yu and martial guard general Huangfu Wuyi, coming one after another from the Eastern Capital to submit, both went to the walls to argue gain and loss.

sentences.zh: 朝廷又賜金券，待以不死。

translations.literal: The court again bestowed a pardon tally, treating him as exempt from death.
translations.idiomatic: The court again granted a pardon tally, promising he would not be put to death.

sentences.zh: 君素卒無降心。

translations.literal: Junsu in the end had no heart to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Junsu in the end would not surrender.

sentences.zh: 其妻又至城下，謂曰：「隋室已亡，何苦取禍？」

translations.literal: His wife also came to the wall and said: "The house of Sui is already destroyed—why torment yourself to court disaster?
translations.idiomatic: His wife also came to the walls and said, "The house of Sui is already gone—why court disaster by holding out?

sentences.zh: 君素曰：「天下事非婦人所知。」

translations.literal: Junsu said: "The affairs of the realm are not for women to know."
translations.idiomatic: Junsu said, "Affairs of the realm are not for women to judge."

sentences.zh: 引弓射之，應弦而倒。

translations.literal: He drew the bow and shot her; she fell at the twang of the string.
translations.idiomatic: He drew his bow and shot her; she fell as the string sounded.

sentences.zh: 君素亦知事必不濟，每言及隋國，未嘗不歔欷。

translations.literal: Junsu also knew matters could not succeed; whenever he spoke of the state of Sui he never failed to sob.
translations.idiomatic: Junsu also knew the cause was lost; whenever he spoke of the Sui state he could not keep from weeping.

sentences.zh: 常謂將士曰：「吾是籓邸舊臣，至於大義，不得不死。

translations.literal: He often told the officers: "I am an old retainer of the princely residence; as to great righteousness, I cannot but die.
translations.idiomatic: He often told his officers, "I am an old retainer of the princely house; on great righteousness I cannot but die.

sentences.zh: 今谷支數年，食盡，足知天下之事。

translations.literal: Now grain has supported us for years; it is exhausted—enough to know how things stand under heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Our grain has held out for years; now it is gone—enough to know how the realm stands.

sentences.zh: 必隋室傾敗，天命有歸，吾當斷頭以付諸君。」

translations.literal: The house of Sui must surely collapse; mandate has its destination; I will give you my severed head.
translations.idiomatic: The house of Sui must fall; Heaven's mandate has its lord; I will give you my severed head.

sentences.zh: 後頗得江都傾覆消息，又糧盡，男女相食，眾心離駭。

translations.literal: Later they received word that Jiangdu had fallen; grain too was gone; men and women ate one another; hearts scattered in terror.
translations.idiomatic: Later word came that Jiangdu had fallen; grain ran out; men and women ate one another; morale collapsed in terror.

sentences.zh: 白虹降於府門，兵器之端，夜皆光見。

translations.literal: A white rainbow descended on the prefecture gate; the tips of weapons at night all shone with light.
translations.idiomatic: A white rainbow descended on the prefectural gate; weapon points gleamed by night.

sentences.zh: 月餘，君素為左右所害。

translations.literal: After more than a month Junsu was killed by those at his side.
translations.idiomatic: After more than a month Junsu was killed by his own men.

sentences.zh: 陳孝意、張季珣、杜松贇，並以誠節顯。

translations.literal: Chen Xiaoyi, Zhang Jixun, and Du Songyun—all showed forth by sincere integrity.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Xiaoyi, Zhang Jixun, and Du Songyun were all famed for steadfast loyalty.

sentences.zh: 孝意，河東人。

translations.literal: Xiaoyi was a man of Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaoyi was a native of Hedong.

sentences.zh: 大業初，為魯郡司法書佐，郡內號為廉平。

translations.literal: Early in Daye he was judicial clerk of Lu Commandery; within the commandery he was called upright and fair.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Daye he served as judicial clerk of Lu Commandery; the commandery called him upright and fair.

sentences.zh: 太守蘇威嘗欲殺一囚，孝意固諫，不許。

translations.literal: The governor Su Wei once wished to execute a prisoner; Xiaoyi firmly remonstrated and would not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: Governor Su Wei once wished to execute a prisoner; Xiaoyi firmly remonstrated and would not allow it.

sentences.zh: 孝意因解衣先受死。

translations.literal: Xiaoyi thereupon removed his robe to accept death first.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaoyi thereupon stripped his robe to accept execution first.

sentences.zh: 良久，威意乃解，謝而遣之，漸加禮敬。

translations.literal: After a long while Wei's mind relented; he apologized and sent him away, and gradually showed him increased respect.
translations.idiomatic: After a long while Wei relented, apologized, and released him, and gradually treated him with greater respect.

sentences.zh: 及威為納言，奏孝意為侍御史。

translations.literal: When Wei became Counselor-in-Chief he memorialized to appoint Xiaoyi supervising censor.
translations.idiomatic: When Wei became Counselor-in-Chief he recommended Xiaoyi as supervising censor.

sentences.zh: 後以父憂去職，居喪過禮，有白鹿馴擾其廬，時人以為孝感。

translations.literal: Later on father's mourning he left office; his observance of mourning exceeded the rites; a white deer came tamely to his hut, and people of the time took it as filial response.
translations.idiomatic: Later he left office for his father's mourning; his observance exceeded the rites; a white deer came tamely to his hut, and people took it as filial response from Heaven.

sentences.zh: 尋起授雁門郡丞。

translations.literal: Soon he was recalled and appointed assistant governor of Yanmen Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon recalled and appointed assistant governor of Yanmen Commandery.

sentences.zh: 在郡菜食齋居，朝夕哀臨，每一發聲，未嘗不絕倒。

translations.literal: In the commandery he ate vegetables and dwelt in seclusion, morning and evening mourning at the coffin; each time he gave voice he invariably collapsed insensible.
translations.idiomatic: In the commandery he ate plain food and lived in seclusion, mourning morning and evening at the coffin; each time he cried out he would collapse insensible.

sentences.zh: 柴毀骨立，見者哀之。

translations.literal: His frame was wasted to the bone by grief; those who saw him mourned for him.
translations.idiomatic: Grief wasted him to the bone; all who saw him were moved to pity.

sentences.zh: 時長吏多贓汙，孝意清節彌厲。

translations.literal: At the time senior officials were mostly corrupt; Xiaoyi's integrity grew ever sterner.
translations.idiomatic: Senior officials were mostly corrupt; Xiaoyi's integrity grew ever sterner.

sentences.zh: 發奸摘伏，動若有神，吏人稱之。

translations.literal: In exposing wrongdoing and detecting hidden guilt his movements were as if spirit-aided; clerks and people praised him.
translations.idiomatic: In exposing crime and uncovering hidden guilt he seemed spirit-aided; clerks and people praised him.

sentences.zh: 煬帝幸江都，馬邑劉武周殺太守王仁恭作亂，前郡丞楊長仁、雁門令王鹈隺等謀應賊。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yang went to Jiangdu, at Mayi Liu Wuzhou killed the governor Wang Rengong and rebelled; the former assistant governor Yang Changren, the magistrate of Yanmen Wang Ehu, and others plotted to join the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yang went to Jiangdu, at Mayi Liu Wuzhou killed Governor Wang Rengong and rebelled; former assistant governor Yang Changren, Yanmen magistrate Wang Ehu, and others plotted to side with the rebels.

sentences.zh: 孝意知之，族滅其家，郡中戰慄。

translations.literal: Xiaoyi learned of it and exterminated their families; the whole commandery trembled.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaoyi learned of it and wiped out their families; the whole commandery trembled.

sentences.zh: 俄而武周來攻，孝意拒之，每致克捷。

translations.literal: Before long Wuzhou came to attack; Xiaoyi resisted him and each time won victory.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Wuzhou attacked; Xiaoyi resisted and won repeated victories.

sentences.zh: 但孤城無援，而孝意誓以必死。

translations.literal: But the lone city had no aid, and Xiaoyi vowed to die.
translations.idiomatic: But the isolated city had no relief, and Xiaoyi vowed to die.

sentences.zh: 亦知帝必不反，每旦夕向詔敕庫俯伏涕流，悲動左右。

translations.literal: He also knew the emperor would surely not return; each dawn and dusk he prostrated himself before the edict store weeping, moving those at his side to grief.
translations.idiomatic: He also knew the emperor would never return; each dawn and dusk he prostrated himself before the edict archive weeping, moving all around him.

sentences.zh: 糧盡，為校尉張世倫所殺，以城歸武周。

translations.literal: When grain was gone he was killed by the commandant Zhang Shilun, who surrendered the city to Wuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When grain ran out, commandant Zhang Shilun killed him and surrendered the city to Wuzhou.

sentences.zh: 張季珣，京兆人。

translations.literal: Zhang Jixun was a man of Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jixun was a native of Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 父祥，少為隋文帝所知，引為丞相參軍，累遷并州司馬。

translations.literal: His father Xiang, in youth was known to Emperor Wen of Sui, who drew him in as staff officer to the chancellor, and he rose to be military governor of Bingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: His father Xiang, known in youth to Emperor Wen, was brought in as staff officer to the chancellor and rose to military governor of Bingzhou.

sentences.zh: 及漢王諒反，遣其將劉建攻之，縱火燒其郭下。

translations.literal: When Prince of Han Liang rebelled he sent his general Liu Jian to attack; they set fire and burned below the outer wall.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince of Han Yang Liang rebelled, he sent his general Liu Jian to attack; they set fires below the outer wall.

sentences.zh: 祥見百姓驚駭，其城西有王母廟，登城望之，再拜號泣曰：「百姓何罪，致此焚燒？

translations.literal: Xiang saw the common people in terror; west of the city was the Queen Mother shrine; he ascended the wall and gazed toward it, twice bowing and crying aloud: "What crime have the people committed to suffer this burning?
translations.idiomatic: Xiang saw the people in terror; west of the city stood the Queen Mother shrine; he climbed the wall, gazed toward it, bowed twice, and cried aloud, "What crime have the people committed to suffer this burning?

sentences.zh: 神其有靈，可降雨相救。」

translations.literal: If the spirit has power, send rain to save them.
translations.idiomatic: If the spirit has power, send rain to save them.

sentences.zh: 言訖，廟上雲起，雨降而火遂滅。

translations.literal: When he finished speaking, clouds rose above the shrine; rain fell and the fire was extinguished.
translations.idiomatic: As he finished, clouds rose above the shrine; rain fell and the fire went out.

sentences.zh: 士卒感其至誠，莫不用命。

translations.literal: The soldiers were moved by his utmost sincerity; none failed to obey.
translations.idiomatic: The soldiers were moved by his utmost sincerity; none failed to give their all.

sentences.zh: 援軍至，賊退。

translations.literal: Relief troops arrived and the bandits retreated.
translations.idiomatic: Relief arrived and the rebels withdrew.

sentences.zh: 以功授開府。

translations.literal: For merit he was appointed Defender of the State.
translations.idiomatic: For his merit he was appointed Defender of the State.

sentences.zh: 後卒于都水監。

translations.literal: Later he died in the office of Director of Waterways.
translations.idiomatic: He later died in office as Director of Waterways.

sentences.zh: 季珣少慷慨，有志節。

translations.literal: Jixun in youth was ardent and had resolve.
translations.idiomatic: Jixun in youth was ardent and high-minded.

sentences.zh: 大業末，為鷹揚郎將。

translations.literal: At the end of Daye he served as Eagle-Flying Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Daye he served as Eagle-Flying Commandant.

sentences.zh: 所居據箕山為固，與洛口接。

translations.literal: Where he dwelt he held Mount Ji as his stronghold, adjoining Luokou.
translations.idiomatic: He made his base on Mount Ji, which linked him to Luokou.

sentences.zh: 及李密陷倉城，遣兵呼之。

translations.literal: When Li Mi took Cangcheng he sent troops to summon him.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Mi captured Cangcheng, he sent troops to summon him.

sentences.zh: 季珣大罵。

translations.literal: Jixun reviled them loudly.
translations.idiomatic: Jixun answered with a torrent of curses.

sentences.zh: 密怒，攻之，連年不能克。

translations.literal: Mi was enraged and attacked; for years he could not take it.
translations.idiomatic: Li Mi flew into a rage and attacked, yet for years he could not overcome the place.

sentences.zh: 經三年，資用盡，無薪，徹屋而爨，人皆穴處。

translations.literal: After three years supplies were exhausted; there was no firewood; they tore down houses to cook; all lived in burrows.
translations.idiomatic: Three years on, stores were spent, firewood gone; they stripped houses for fuel and everyone dwelt in dug-out shelters.

sentences.zh: 季珣撫之，一無離叛。

translations.literal: Jixun comforted them; not one deserted.
translations.idiomatic: Jixun steadied them, and not a man deserted.

sentences.zh: 後士卒饑羸，為密所陷。

translations.literal: Later the soldiers, starving and wasted, were overcome by Mi.
translations.idiomatic: In time his troops, starved and enfeebled, fell to Li Mi.

sentences.zh: 季珣坐査事，顏色自若，密遣兵禽送之。

translations.literal: Jixun sat handling affairs, his countenance unchanged; Mi sent troops to seize and escort him.
translations.idiomatic: Jixun sat as if at his desk on routine business, his face unaltered; Li Mi sent men to seize him and bring him in.

sentences.zh: 群賊曳令拜密。

translations.literal: The rebel host dragged him and ordered him to bow to Mi.
translations.idiomatic: The rebel throng hauled him forward and forced him to bow to Li Mi.

sentences.zh: 季珣曰：「吾雖敗軍將，猶是天子爪牙臣，何容拜賊！」

translations.literal: Jixun said: "Though I am a defeated general, I am still the Son of Heaven's claw-and-fang minister—how could I bow to bandits!"
translations.idiomatic: Jixun said, "I may be a beaten general, yet I am still a fang-and-claw servant of the Son of Heaven—how could I bow to rebels!"

sentences.zh: 密壯而釋之。

translations.literal: Mi admired him and released him.
translations.idiomatic: Li Mi was impressed and let him go.

sentences.zh: 翟讓從求金不得，殺之。

translations.literal: Zhai Rang followed to ask for gold and did not obtain it; he killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhai Rang came demanding gold; when Jixun refused, he killed him.

sentences.zh: 其弟仲琰，為上洛令。

translations.literal: His younger brother Zhongyan served as magistrate of Shangluo.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Zhongyan was magistrate of Shangluo.

sentences.zh: 及義兵起，城守，部下殺之以歸義。

translations.literal: When the righteous armies arose he defended the city; his subordinates killed him to submit to the righteous cause.
translations.idiomatic: When the loyalist armies rose, he held the city until his own men slew him to surrender to the cause.

sentences.zh: 仲琰弟幼琮，為千牛左右。

translations.literal: Zhongyan's younger brother Youcong served as attendant of the Thousand-Ox Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongyan's younger brother Youcong served in the Thousand-Ox Guard.

sentences.zh: 宇文化及亂，遇害。

translations.literal: In Yuwen Huaji's rebellion he met calamity.
translations.idiomatic: He perished in Yuwen Huaji's coup.

sentences.zh: 季珣世忠烈，兄弟俱死國難，論者賢之。

translations.literal: The Jixun family for generations was fiercely loyal; the brothers all died in the state's calamity; commentators held them worthy.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhang house had been loyal for generations; the brothers all died in the nation's ruin, and commentators pronounced them worthy.

sentences.zh: 杜松贇，北海人也。

translations.literal: Du Songyun was a man of Beihai.
translations.idiomatic: Du Songyun was a native of Beihai.

sentences.zh: 性剛烈，重名義。

translations.literal: By nature he was stern and fierce; he prized reputation and righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: Fierce by nature, he set great store by honor and duty.

sentences.zh: 為石門府隊正。

translations.literal: He served as squad leader of Shimen Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He served as squad leader of Shimen Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 大業末，楊厚來攻北海縣，松贇覘賊被執。

translations.literal: At the end of Daye, Yang Hou came to attack Beihai County; Songyun, scouting the bandits, was seized.
translations.idiomatic: Late in the Daye reign, Yang Hou attacked Beihai County; while scouting the rebels, Songyun was captured.

sentences.zh: 使謂城中，云「郡兵已破，宜早歸降」，松贇偽許之。

translations.literal: They had him tell the city, saying "The prefectural troops are broken; you should submit early"; Songyun falsely agreed.
translations.idiomatic: They made him call to the city that the prefectural army was routed and surrender was due; Songyun pretended to comply.

sentences.zh: 既至城下，大呼曰：「我邂逅被執，非力屈也。

translations.literal: When he reached the foot of the wall he shouted aloud: "I was seized by chance encounter—it is not that my strength yielded.
translations.idiomatic: At the wall he cried out, "I was taken by mischance, not because I yielded!

sentences.zh: 官軍大來，賊旦暮禽翦。」

translations.literal: The government army is coming in force; the bandits will be captured and cut down within days."
translations.idiomatic: The imperial host is on the march—the rebels will be rounded up and destroyed any day now."

sentences.zh: 賊以刀築其口，引之去。

translations.literal: The bandits rammed his mouth with a blade and led him away.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels silenced him with a blade at his mouth and dragged him off.

sentences.zh: 松贇罵厚曰：「老賊何敢辱賢良！」

translations.literal: Songyun reviled Hou, saying: "Old bandit—how dare you insult a worthy gentleman!"
translations.idiomatic: Songyun cursed Yang Hou: "You old rebel—how dare you shame a man of worth!"

sentences.zh: 言未卒，賊斷其腰。

translations.literal: Before he finished speaking the bandits severed him at the waist.
translations.idiomatic: His words were not out before the rebels cut him in two at the waist.

sentences.zh: 城中望之，莫不流涕扼腕，銳氣益倍，北海卒完。

translations.literal: Those in the city who watched it all wept and wrung their wrists; fighting spirit doubled; Beihai in the end was preserved.
translations.idiomatic: Watching from the walls, none could hold back tears or clenched fists; their ardor doubled, and Beihai held firm to the end.

sentences.zh: 優贈朝請大夫、本郡通守。

translations.literal: He was posthumously honored as Gentleman Attendant at Court and overseer of his native commandery.
translations.idiomatic: The court posthumously enfeoffed him as Gentleman Attendant at Court and overseer of his home commandery.

sentences.zh: 郭世俊，字弘乂，太原文水人也。

translations.literal: Guo Shijun, style name Hongyi, was a man of Wenshui in Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Shijun, styled Hongyi, came from Wenshui in Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 家門雍睦，七世同居，犬豕同乳，鳥鵲同巢，時人以為義感之應。

translations.literal: The household was harmonious; seven generations dwelt together; dogs and pigs nursed together, birds and magpies shared nests; people of the time took it as a response to their righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: His clan lived in harmony—seven generations under one roof; dogs and pigs suckled together, birds and magpies nested as one; contemporaries saw it as heaven's answer to their virtue.

sentences.zh: 州縣上其事，隋文帝遣平昌公宇文幹詣其家勞問。

translations.literal: The prefecture and county reported the matter; Emperor Wen of Sui sent Duke of Pingchang Yuwen Gan to his home to console and inquire.
translations.idiomatic: Local officials reported it, and Emperor Wen sent Duke of Pingchang Yuwen Gan to visit the household with imperial praise.

sentences.zh: 尚書侍御史柳彧巡省河北，表其門閭。

translations.literal: Secretariat Attendant Censor Liu Yu toured Hebei and memorialized honor for their gate.
translations.idiomatic: Secretariat Attendant Censor Liu Yu, on circuit in Hebei, petitioned to honor their gate.

sentences.zh: 漢王諒為并州總管，聞而嘉歎，賜其兄弟二十餘人衣各一襲。

translations.literal: Prince of Han Liang was governor-general of Bingzhou; hearing of it he praised and sighed, and bestowed on his more than twenty brothers one suit of clothes each.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Han Yang Liang, governor-general of Bingzhou, heard and marveled, and gave each of the more than twenty brothers a full suit of robes.

sentences.zh: 郎方貴，淮南人也。

translations.literal: Lang Fanggui was a man of Huainan.
translations.idiomatic: Lang Fanggui was a native of Huainan.

sentences.zh: 少有志尚，與從父弟雙貴同居。

translations.literal: In youth he had lofty resolve; he dwelt together with his paternal cousin Shuanggui.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he was high-minded and lived with his cousin Shuanggui.

sentences.zh: 隋開皇中，方貴常于淮水津所寄渡，舟人怒之，撾方貴臂折。

translations.literal: In the Kaihuang era of Sui, Fanggui often crossed by ferry on the Huai; the boatman, enraged, beat Fanggui and broke his arm.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaihuang, Fanggui often crossed the Huai at the ferry; a boatman, furious, beat him and broke his arm.

sentences.zh: 至家，雙貴問知之，恚恨，遂向津，毆殺船人。

translations.literal: When he reached home Shuanggui learned of it, burned with hatred, went straight to the ferry, and beat the boatman to death.
translations.idiomatic: Home again, Shuanggui learned what had happened, seethed with rage, went to the ferry, and killed the boatman.

sentences.zh: 津者執送之。

translations.literal: The ferry officials seized and sent him in.
translations.idiomatic: Ferry officials arrested him and turned him over.

sentences.zh: 縣以方貴為首，當死，雙貴從坐，當流。

translations.literal: The county held Fanggui as principal and liable to death; Shuanggui as accomplice was liable to exile.
translations.idiomatic: The county ruled Fanggui the principal offender, punishable by death, and Shuanggui an accomplice, punishable by exile.

sentences.zh: 兄弟爭為首坐，縣司不能斷，送詣州。

translations.literal: The brothers disputed who was principal; the county office could not decide and sent them to the prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Each brother insisted he was the principal offender; the county could not decide and referred the case to the prefecture.

sentences.zh: 兄弟各引死，州不能定。

translations.literal: Each brother claimed the death penalty; the prefecture could not settle it.
translations.idiomatic: Each claimed the capital charge, and the prefecture could not settle it.

sentences.zh: 二人爭欲赴水死。

translations.literal: The two disputed, each wishing to rush into the water and die.
translations.idiomatic: Both strove to throw themselves into the river and die.

sentences.zh: 州以狀聞。

translations.literal: The prefecture reported the case upward.
translations.idiomatic: The prefecture reported the matter to the throne.

sentences.zh: 上聞，異之，特原其罪，表其門閭，賜物百段。

translations.literal: The emperor heard and marveled; he specially pardoned their crime, honored their gate, and bestowed a hundred lengths of goods.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor heard and was moved; he specially pardoned them, honored their gate, and granted a hundred lengths of goods.

sentences.zh: 後為州主簿。

translations.literal: Later he served as chief clerk of the prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He later served as chief clerk of the prefecture.

sentences.zh: 論曰：於什門等或臨危不撓，視死如歸；

translations.literal: The commentary says: Yu Shimen and the like—some, facing peril, did not bend and regarded death as returning home;
translations.idiomatic: Commentary: Men such as Yu Shimen, facing peril, did not bend; some looked on death as a homecoming;

sentences.zh: 或赴險如夷，唯義有所在。

translations.literal: some went into danger as onto level ground—only where righteousness lay.
translations.idiomatic: others walked into danger as if on level ground—each moved only where duty called.

sentences.zh: 其大則光國隆家，其小則損己利物。

translations.literal: In the large they illumined the state and exalted the clan; in the small they harmed themselves to benefit others.
translations.idiomatic: At their grandest they brightened the realm and raised their houses; at their humblest they harmed themselves to help others.

sentences.zh: 故其盛烈所著，與河海而爭流；

translations.literal: Thus the splendor they left vies in flow with rivers and seas;
translations.idiomatic: Their blazing deeds, set down in record, race the rivers and seas in their rush;

sentences.zh: 峻節所標，共竹柏而俱茂。

translations.literal: the lofty integrity they marked flourishes together with bamboo and cypress.
translations.idiomatic: the stern integrity they marked stands evergreen with bamboo and pine.

sentences.zh: 並蹈履之所致，身沒名立，豈徒然也！

translations.literal: All were achieved by treading the path; the body perished yet the name was established—was it for nothing!
translations.idiomatic: All this came of walking the path: bodies fell, names rose—and surely not in vain!
